chapters.title: Chapter 697 - Prismar
chapters.content:
Drawn towards the temple that was overgrown with the surrounding plants, Jennifer approached it slowly without even realising the same.
The closer she came, the stronger the pull became, and it was the moment she was right above the temple that she noticed a portal close to the entrance.
This made her turn towards Jason, who had followed her quietly.
"I think that's the inheritance site I want to enter. There is only one problem…" She had been excited about the inheritance site, only to realise that Jason was still with her.
She had to protect him, but that wouldn't work if her instincts about only those with three cultivation energies being able to enter the temple including her were to be true.
The moment Jason saw the temple, he realised that it hadn't been used for a very long time, which meant that not many beings had managed to enter it.
At the same time, the fact that Jennifer was pulled towards it, indicated that she was perfectly suitable for the inheritance.
If one was pulled towards a specific inheritance site, it was said that one was not only perfectly suitable for the final inheritance but also highly likely to pass all trials, as long as no unforeseen event happened.
There were many beings that were suitable for specific inheritances, but in the end, most wouldn't survive the trial's dangers.
As such, Jason knew that Jennifer had to enter the Temple Inheritance site.
"I won't be able to enter it with you, I think" He simply guessed, to which Jennifer nodded her head in uncertainty.
Initially, Jason would have found this annoying, but instead of acting up, he just nodded his head
"I will be fine. If I cannot follow you, I should just cultivate, and advance to the Prismar stage. Afterward, I will be able to take care of myself!"
Jason was not sure how true this was, but he didn't want to hold Jennifer back. As such, he just said that he would be fine without her around him.
That didn't have to be true, but there was something he had up his sleeves, allowing him to take care of a few nuisances.
Due to this, he was prepared to venture out alone, at least to a certain extent.
Jennifer noticed that Jason was confident in himself, which eased her mind as she spoke in a faint voice.
"Thank you!"
Afterward, she slowly approached the portal, and reached for it, brushing her fingers across it without showing any hesitation.
'She is really restless about the Inheritance...that's something new.' Jason thought as he saw how Jennifer reacted and disappeared inside the portal before he could even wish her good luck.
She didn't even take a single backward glance which caused Jason to sigh before he approached the portal as well.
Yet, the moment he touched it, the portal repelled him as he had already expected.
This caused him to issue another sigh before he took a look at the temple's inside.
'There is a concealment, that's great!'
The entire temple was concealed, which originated from the material out of which it was constructed.
Jason had never seen stones like that before but they allowed the three cultivation energies to enter the temple even through them, which was strictly one way, the walls prevented them from leaving.
This was interesting and extremely useful for Jason, who wanted to stay inside the temple, so as to conceal his energy ripples and avoid unnecessary conflicts if someone were to find him all by himself.
He might be unable to enter the inheritance site inside the temple, but the temple itself was accessible!
Thankful for the opportunity, he momentarily even forgot that he was now alone if one were to exclude his soulbonds.
Petri and Solaris were still clinging to his body, while Spyro was cultivating inside the soul world.
Artemis evolution was also progressing, at a slow, yet steady pace.
Jason was not sure how many months it would take her to finish the entire evolution, but it would be great if it would be over before his time inside Kinra Island would end.
That had many reasons, but the most important one was that his gut feeling told him that he would be in a dire need of her by then.
He was also not sure how long the Tortoise would hibernate, but Luna had told him that the Island would remain at the same location for a duration between six months and an entire year.
As such, he had quite some time to cultivate and possibly even to find his own inheritance.
Because he was weaker than Jennifer, his main focus wouldn't be the Immortal eye. Instead, Jennifer could look for it.
After all, she was her disciple.
He might have received an extremely powerful cultivation technique, but that didn't mean he would have to act even more reckless than he already did by entering Kinra Island while being at the Lique stage.
In the end, that could already be considered a life-threatening action, with an extremely high death rate. It was almost suicidal, if Jason were to be honest to himself!
Fortunately, this would change soon because Jason focused on cultivating the moment he entered the basement of the temple.
Seated on the ground, Jason greedily absorbed the mana that was unable to escape the temple and used it to empower the creation of the first solidified prismarine crystal.
There were not many things he had to do in order to solidify a prismarine crystal, but it was deemed as extremely complex.
However, using the three Stigma and his Celestia aura to support the solidification process, the complex mechanisms seemed to vanish.
Everything went smoothly, and there was not even a single issue Jason encountered.
Normally, it was said that the creation of the first solidified prismarine crystal was the most difficult because many made small rookie mistakes, forcing them to disintegrate the flawed product once again.
This would force them to stay at the peak of the Lique stage before they had replenished the used up mana drops.
Fortunately, nothing of that happened to Jason, and he was able to create his first prismarine crystal, only one month later.
He did everything slowly, focusing on the smallest details, while his Stigma and aura were intertwining with the final product, seemingly strengthening it.
The faint traces of his father's divinity that had been annexed and merged with his own body influenced the creation of the solidified prismarine crystal.
Through this, it became firmer, and he was able to further increase the circulation speed of mana.
But? most importantly, it was more effective and stronger than a normal prismarine crystal by around four times!!
When Jason noticed this, he was shocked because he had expected the solidified prismarine crystal to be only three times stronger than the norm.
That was solely based on the strength of his unique mana drops that required thrice the mana to be compressed into a single drop.
Never could he have imagined that the divinity that swept through his body, which Jason had never really noticed, was the cause of all of this.
Meanwhile, Solaris was about to create its second prismarine crystal, and Petri had entered the 9th Lique stage.
During the last month, even Spyro had almost created its stigma, using enormous amounts of soul energy and spirit force.
Meanwhile, what Jason didn't realise either, was that many things happened on the outside of the temple, and even inside!
He had been in a fully focused state, and owing to that, he hadn't even noticed the temple's reaction to his advancement to the Prismar stage.
To Jason, the advancement hadn't been anything special, and only the end result shocked him extremely.
Because of his ignorance, he couldn't even understand that he was the reason for what was about to happen at any moment.
As if on cue, the entire temple began to shake, the moment Jason advanced to the Prismar stage. His Celestia aura was fully unleashed, enveloping him tightly, indicating the emergence of a new being at the Prismar stage.
Just as the temple shook, Jason released something that caused his vibrant eyes to bulge as he lifted his head, facing the Temple inheritance's portal.
"Am I...being pulled towards it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 698 - Threat
chapters.content:
"Am I...being pulled towards it?" Jason mumbled the moment he felt a strong suction force from the portal that was less than 50 meters above him.
However, only a moment later, Jason noticed that his assumption was not exactly correct.
He was pulled towards the portal right in front of him, but at the same time, Jason felt that his body was drawn in every single direction.
Because of that, he couldn't help but feel astonished as he wondered whether his mind was playing tricks on him, or if his thought was correct.
'Am I being pulled towards all inheritances and not just one?'
This shouldn't be the case because the majority of inheritances were not suitable to him, and Jason was completely aware of this.
Nevertheless, what he felt was neither an illusion nor a trick.
As such, instead of wondering if he was truly pulled towards all inheritances, Jason asked himself why this should be the case.
'Is it because of my aura or the fact that I advanced to the Prismar stage?' The latter seemed to be wrong, but the former was not exactly a reason that should allow him to enter all kinds of inheritance sites either.
Unfortunately, the two reasons he had named were the only things that had happened during the entire month that had been deadly silent in all other respects.
In the end, the Celestia aura was the most reasonable answer he could come up with, and Jason began to wonder how his presence had been noticed.
'During my advancement, the Celestia aura shouldn't have been strong enough to envelop the entire island. That would be madness. Does that mean that all Inheritances are somehow connected and that my aura reaches every single inheritance site?'
Right now, Jason was simply trying to join the dots, but nothing really made sense.
As such, he could only stop making assumptions for now.
Instead, Jason approached the surface, as the bright sun shone on his fair skin.
Looking around, he saw that not a single living being was in the vicinity, which was more confusing than reassuring.
However, instead of worrying about it, Jason grew eager to test how it was possible to fly at the Prismar stage, without the use of wings!
That was a privilege of beings at the Prismar stage, and Jason wanted to make use of it.
With that thought in mind, he didn't use his wings and tried to follow the instructions he had been given some time ago.
'Jennifer said that the solidified prismarine crystal can be utilised to negate the gravitational force to some extent, so how am I going to do that?'
Thanks to the information he had been provided by Jennifer during the last few days before she entered the portal, it didn't take long for Jason to figure out how flying without wings worked.
His speed was not extraordinarily fast, but much faster than others who had the same cultivation base as him.
That was owing to his unique prismarine crystal that was intertwined with golden and silver strands.
Nevertheless, he was still slower than with the use of Artemis or Solaris' wings.
As such, he returned to the temple before looking at the portal.
"If I'm drawn towards the portal, I should be able to enter it...but is that really what I want to do?" Jason mumbled quietly while staring at the portal.
Once he entered, there was no way that he would be able to return easily.
As such, it was necessary for him to pass a few trials beforehand.
Thus, he would have to make a thorough decision because it was possible that some trials would take up too much of his time.
Even if he had told Luna that he would follow Jennifer, he was also slightly egoistic and wanted to find an inheritance for himself too.
Nevertheless, he could tell that Jennifer was more important to him than just any inheritance.
This realisation caused Jason to ask himself since when had his thoughts about the young woman changed to this.
'Is she already as important as my late masters had been to me?' He wondered, only to smile sadly at the thought of Shane and Dalia.
Nevertheless, he noticed that he couldn't answer the question because he was not sure how much he cared about Jennifer.
Such thoughts were never something he had bothered about before. As such, they were new and completely unfamiliar to him.
However, before he was able to continue thinking about Jennifer, or the fact that it might be safer for him to follow her, multiple things happened at the same time.
First, at the thought of Jennifer, he got a bad feeling, and sensing something behind him, he instinctively turned around, only to see a total of four individuals that approached the Temple inheritance.
'What the hell are those?!' Jason almost exclaimed as he saw four humanoid beings that had all awakened three cultivation veins.
Seeing this, he felt jealous for a short moment, only to realise that he had no time to waste.
Never in his life would he ignore a premonition, and both the thought of Jennifer and the four individuals he saw through the walls owing to his Emperor Eyes, made him have a premonition.
Despite that, he didn't immediately enter the portal of the Temple inheritance.
Instead, he retracted his mana fluctuations, the Celestia aura, and Stigma, while Petri and Solaris were forced to return to the soul world.
Sensing Jason's emotional chaos they didn't even try to resist knowing that it would only enrage Jason.
With his entire being concealed, Jason couldn't be found if nobody was actively searching for him.
However, his assumption was proved incorrect as the four individuals who were all at the peak of the Prismar stage had just entered the Temple, the moment Jason hid behind a big pillar.
A hue filled with a raging fury could be seen around all four beings, which told Jason that he shouldn't offend them if possible.
They were noticeably enraged, which he could not only see according to the hue but also their conversation that reverberated through the entire Temple.
"It took quite a while before this fucking Tortoise resurfaced...but why does it have to be in such a weird area? Without the help of our Ancestors, we would have never found it…"
One of the beings said, using a unique sound in between his speech.
"Don't complain, idiot. Let's retrieve everything traitor Kairn stole and return to our origin planet. This place is not good for us. It's just a waste of time!!"
A second voice said, only for the third being to nod his head.
"I agree, let's finish everything as quickly as possible. If we wouldn't have been punished for accidentally killing a few 'prodigies' at the Mikalda gathering, there is no way we would be here, right?"
Sighing deeply, the third being seemed to feel as if they had been punished for no credible reason.
However, a fourth voice that sounded extremely arrogant resounded in the temple as he remarked,
"Who told these idiots to be so weak? They should have known that offending us won't do them any good!
That's what they get for underestimating us, Preactors!"
When Jason heard all of this, he was confused, but at the same time, he knew that Jennifer was in danger, which caused him to nervously bite his lower lip.

chapters.title: Chapter 699 - First Trial
chapters.content:
The Preactor race, which was the name Jason assumed them to have, was extremely weird.
What he was able to see through the pillar using his Emperor Eyes was more than enough for him to be astonished, but that only increased as he took a peek, the moment they entered the portal.
All four of them had greyish skin, necks that were more than 30 centimeters long, sharp teeth, a flat nose, their back was covered with scales, but the most important aspect was their seemingly endless anger, and three activated cultivation veins.
Based on what he had overheard, Jason was able to figure out that the Inheritance came from the Preactor race, or to be precise someone who had betrayed them.
At the same time, it hadn't been difficult to tell that the four Preactors were prodigies, and underestimated because of their age.
Adding it to the fact that they didn't seem to like Manyr, or Kinra Island, he concluded that their race must be extremely strong.
They had been talking about their origin planet and how it was better to stay there.
As such, Jason comprehended that their home planet was better for them to cultivate.
A punishment of entering an Inheritance site was something Jason had never heard, but based on the Preactors' confidence, he could easily tell that they didn't consider anything about the inheritance site as dangerous.
This was not good, and Jason became only more worried about Jennifer.
Unfortunately, he didn't know whether the first trial inside the Inheritance site threw all participants in one area, or if it was a trial one had to solve alone.
With that unknown factor in mind, Jason had to wait for some time before he rushed to the portal, ignoring the minuscule possibility that the pulling force he felt was just an illusion.
Believing his body, Jason rushed through the portal, only to feel the familiar sensation of being teleported to a different location.
Surrounded by darkness that was pierced through by bright shining stars, Jason could only hope that Jennifer had already passed a few trials, otherwise, everything would become extremely burdensome.
Suddenly, he heard a robotic voice inside his head, originating from the trials.
[Welcome to the Legacy trials of the Supreme Magician.]
[Requirement of owning all three cultivation veins has not been met! Instead, Unique requirement has been met.
[Welcome youngling of the Primordials!]
[Prismar stage- One small (highly compressed) prismarine crystal detected! Level of Difficulty, adjusted!]
The multitude of messages overlapped inside his mind, and Jason could barely decipher them by guessing what he was supposed to make of it.
He didn't know what Primordials had to do with him, but Jason simply wanted to connect that with the fact that he was half Celestia.
However, it could also have something to do with Primal humans. Because of that, he was not sure where to put Primordial in the evolutionary cycle of humans.
In the end, what was more important was that he was able to enter the Inheritance site, or Legacy trials, which was the name the robotic voice gave to the place he was just about to enter.
The difficulty of his missions was tweaked, which was good to know.
As such, he might be able to use his high strength to pass the trials in a flash.
Unfortunately, it was not as easy as he was hoping for.
In fact, Jason had yet to realise that certain trials were bound to be more difficult than he could have ever expected.
He was not sure how much time had passed, but when he emerged on the other side of the portal, Jason found himself in the middle of a lush forest that had dense vegetation consisting of a variety of plants.
[Trial-1: Defeat all beasts below the 'Mid-1st threshold of the Prismar stage' - 72 hours left!]
The robotic voice resounded in his mind again, but instead of thinking about the mission, Jason wondered where the voice came from.
There was no thread of energy that led towards him or anything like that, and it was just the voice inside his head.
It felt weird, but Jason could tell that the voice meant him no harm.
Because of that, he was able to calm down really quickly.
Taking a look around, the Emperor Eyes inspected his entire surroundings at a glance.
This gave him the opportunity to figure out whether there were any dangers around him or not.
Fortunately, there was no strong beast in his immediate surroundings giving Jason some time to figure out what he had to do.
'I have three days to kill every beast with less than four solidified prismarine crystals. However, this also means that there are stronger beasts!'
Jason quickly concluded the mission's details, with the most important aspect being that there were stronger beasts in his surroundings.
As such, he had to pay attention to the beasts he encountered.
Nevertheless, he didn't even think of taking it slow because he had to meet Jennifer as quickly as possible.
She had a head start of an entire month, which was good because it would take some time before Jennifer would encounter the Preactors, but at the same time, it was annoying because Jason had to charge up to her.
'First, I shall find out what and how many beasts are there in my surroundings, and how large the space around me is!'
Jason didn't believe that he was on an ordinary planet right now, otherwise, it wouldn't make sense for him to be asked to defeat all beasts.
As such, he had to be in a secret realm or a restricted zone in which he had to defeat the beasts.
Thus, Jason exerted the Floating Sky technique before he rushed through the lush forest, which had dense foliage that didn't even let sun rays pass through it and touch the ground.
It was only at the moment he began to run that he noticed how much stronger he had become.
Before, he hadn't felt a big difference, but through the solidified prismarine crystal, many things about his mana control, and circulation had changed, let alone the fact that his entire being had been enhanced.
Earlier, the 10,000 highly compressed liquefied drops of mana were equal to 30,000 common liquefied drops of mana.
Meanwhile, a normal solidified prismarine crystal was equivalent to 25,000 drops of liquefied mana.
However, now after Jason had advanced to the Prismar stage, solidifying his highly compressed liquefied drops of mana, the special prismarine crystal he had was equivalent to the strength of more than 100,000 drops of normal compressed liquefied mana drops!
Adding his soulbond's amplification that was almost negligible in face of the insanely high amount of strength he had acquired, Jason couldn't help but feel amazing as he rushed through the forest.
Ignoring the beasts he passed, Jason simply tried to increase his speed to the highest possible as he released his Celestia aura and Stigma, improving the Floating Sky movement technique's efficiency.
Through this, only a few hours passed before he was done inspecting the entire dome-like space he had entered.
'So...it's like that!' Jason thought with a scheming smile on his face as he returned to the center of the dome.
Without truly caring about the dangers he brought forward, he set the entire forest on fire as he threw fingertip-sized flames in all directions.
He knew the position of all beasts that had four or even five prismarine crystals, but Jason was not really fazed by them.
As long as he gave his utmost efforts, he was confident of being able to defeat them.
Thus, no beast inside the restricted space was strong enough to face him head-on.
At least that was what he expected, ignoring the important factor that beasts were also beings that could have unique traits and abilities!

chapters.title: Chapter 700 - Fused Beast
chapters.content:
Burning down the forest was only a good decision as long as he was confident in defeating all kinds of opponents inside the small space he found himself in.
Fortunately, that was the case, and Jason was eager to finish the first trial quickly.
Using his Emperor Eyes, he had been able to figure out the vast majority of the inhabiting beast's strong traits, even without intently looking at them.
Thus, only a few hours had passed before the vast majority of the forest was reduced to ashes.
Yet, at the same time, Jason hadn't remained idle.
Rather, he had already initiated his attack, killing hundreds of beasts.
With his extraordinary strength, he looked unstoppable, and he didn't face many issues with his prismarine crystal, his soulbond's amplification, and multiple more factors that increased his strength further.
Every single cell in his body was surging with seemingly endless power, and Jason didn't even notice that he was tirelessly attacking the beasts, without paying any attention whatsoever to the kind of beast he was fighting.
Adrenaline was kicking in coupled with the addicting sensation of being able to overwhelm opponents he had been unable to kill, or even injure before.
Thus, the more he fought, the broader his smile became.
At least until he reached a cavern entrance, from which a purple winged wolf emerged followed by two more wolves that looked exactly the same.
Three meters tall, purple feathered wings, and lightning spreading through their fur.
Yet, the moment they saw Jason, whose Celestia aura and Stigma were already fully unleashed, every single strand of their hair erected.
Before, Jason would have just attacked them recklessly, but he got a bad feeling about the Winged lightning wolves.
The largest one amongst them was four meters in height, and through the Emperor Eyes, Jason could clearly determine that it was a mutation.
Owing to this mutation, it was innately stronger than the rest, but at the same time, he was able to clearly see something unique within the mutated wolf.
Its constitution was different compared to the other two wolves, but it was quite different to his late masters, or anyone else he had encountered with unique constitutions.
Rather, it was something that seemed to be connected to the other two wolves.
The moment the large wolf saw Jason, it howled out, while releasing strong mana currents.
All three wolves had three prismarine crystals within their mana core.
As such, they were weaker than him, because his prismarine crystal had the strength of four normal ones.
Nevertheless, he didn't attack immediately because the mutation his eyes perceived caused him to halt in his tracks.
However, this brief pause led him to lose his upper hand!
Unfortunately, Jason noticed this too late, and the moment the mutated wolf's body began to glow in a faint light, he saw something that shocked him greatly.
At the same time, it made him act instinctively as he summoned Byakur and Solaris.
Simultaneously, Petri entered his mana core, before his reptilian eyes and stigma were fused with Jason.
What Jason saw, was in fact, a fusion between the winged lightning wolves!
The moment the other wolf touched the body of the mutated wolf, they began to merge, enlarging in size while the head and tails grew out of the mutated wolf's body.
That was shocking because Jason had never expected something like that to happen, even less because the fused wolf now had two pairs of heads, tails, wings, and mana cores!!
While the fusion between the two wolves had started, the third wolf was just about to join the fray.
However, Jason, who had already acted instinctively, had emerged in front of it, slashing out with Byakur that was enveloped in a thick layer of Solaris' flames.
The moment Jason acted, his own fusion that took less than a second had been completed, allowing him to activate two Stigmas at the same time.
Other than that, he had fully released the Celestia aura further increasing his mana circulation speed.
As such, after activating the perfect mastery Floating Sky movement technique, Jason didn't even need a full second to reach the lone wolf that didn't expect the young human to react so quickly.
Jason's speed was a shocker owing to which the third wolf was unable to erect its defenses properly.
Thus, Jason could easily slash at the winged lightning wolf forcing it to retreat.
It had to release a tremendous amount of mana which it used to conjure lightning around it.
With that, it could accelerate faster and to a much higher limit.
Unfortunately, Jason was still faster than the wolf, and the race specific weakening curse followed by the petrification and abyssal curse were all much stronger than they had been before he advanced to the Prismar stage.
As such he weakened and paralysed the retreating beast easily with the help of the three curses.
Thus, his overall might had increased to a high level and his agility helped him end the third winged lightning wolf's miserable life without hesitation, beheading it mercilessly.
A fountain of blood gushed out of the severed neck, giving him the chance to turn around, finally facing the fused beast whose fusion was probably still underway.
However, contrary to his expectations it had just finished fusing, only to realise that its brethren had been killed.
Enraged by this, it had already appeared in front of Jason, with a much higher velocity than he expected.
There were only two mana cores with each having three solidified crystals inside, but Jason felt that they were not added together, but it was as if they were multiplied with each other.
Shocked by the beast's pace, he could barely lift Byakur in order to deflect the claw that was ripping through the air, intending to kill him.
When they collided, Jason was not even able to continue standing and was swept off his feet.
As such, he was flung through the air, where he crashed into the ground more than a dozen meters away.
However, instead of lying on the ground, Jason had already manifested Petri's tail through which he had pushed himself up from the ground without the need to use his hands to get back on his feet.
This allowed him to witness the winged two-headed lightning wolf's pace with which it appeared in front of him.
'It is slower than I first thought!' Jason suddenly noticed, giving him the chance to use Solaris in addition to the previous factors in order to increase his speed once again.
With flames bursting out from behind Jason, he was propelled forward, allowing him to evade the wolf's subsequent attacks by a hair's breadth before he had finally adjusted to the weird sensation.
His body was still not accustomed to being several times stronger than before. Even the last dozens of fights hadn't been enough to help him adapt.
As such, he was overjoyed to fight a powerful opponent against which he had to give his utmost efforts to even survive.
It was insane, but that was exactly the thought that flashed through Jason's mind as a bright smile emerged on his face the moment he used the combination of his curses and the abyssal effect to target the wolf with it!
Through this, the dance of life and death of two powerful, fused beings had begun, shaking the small space in which they wreaked havoc.

chapters.title: Chapter 701 - Fight Of The Fused
chapters.content:
With a massive mana consumption, Jason stood facing the winged two-headed lightning wolf, who towered over him with a height of more than four meters.
It was extremely fast and agile, but so was Jason!
Using all means he had, he sent the combination of his curses and the abyssal effect at the wolf that hit it with full force, weakening it much more than he could have hoped for.
As such, Jason couldn't help but feel glad that his attack worked because he would have been much slower than it otherwise.
The two mana cores within the fused wolf's body were releasing a tremendous amount of mana, creating short bursts of lightning that targeted Jason like small snakes that were lunging after their prey.
Though these attacks weren't as lethal as the wolf hoped for owing to its drastically reduced strength hence, Jason was at least able to evade most attacks that would have injured him.
A protective armor was created around him by Petri's due to which Jason was almost completely unaffected by the lightning that lunged after him.
Thus, he could easily pay more attention to launching attacks instead of acting defensively.
It was more complex than he had initially expected, but while adjusting to his enhanced body, Jason couldn't help but be glad that he had already fought against a few beasts before.
They hadn't been a challenge, but that was not important at the moment.
Rather, the current situation forced Jason to overcome his physical strength that was still not perfect.
This helped him even out everything, easing the entire tension that had been accumulated within Jason's body in the time he had cultivated.
Under normal circumstances, cultivating was not burdensome.
Instead, it was a soothing feeling that helped the practitioner stay relaxed.
Unfortunately, this was not the case for the Mythic Essence technique that caused unbearable pain, the entire time one cultivated it.
As such, Jason was tense for the whole time, and only due to Solaris' soothing flames that were often spread through his body was he yet to encounter issues.
Despite that, fighting against an opponent that allowed Jason to go all out was even better to ease his tension, making him feel as if he had regained his freedom.
Owing to this sensation, Jason didn't even notice that the Celestia aura, which had been transmuted through the fusion with Petri, was enlarging while being swept through with his battle intent.
With a radiant smile on his face that was hidden by the scaled armor that covered his entire body, Jason twisted himself the moment he saw compressed lightning currents that shot towards him.
While he tried evading them, the lightning currents devastated the surroundings, stirring up the soil that flew through the air.
At that moment, Jason got an idea.
Being unable to directly attack the winged two-headed lightning wolf, despite the fact that the race specific weakening curse was up and running, Jason didn't hesitate to test out new things.
Owing to this free spirit of experimenting with all kinds of things, Jason manifested Solaris' wings while being fused with Petri, only to conjure both icicles and fireballs which he threw towards the wolf, who didn't even bother to deflect the attacks.
Instead, it enveloped itself in small lightning bolts that crackled and lunged at everything that entered their range.
This was something Jason had already seen before. Thus, he had already expected this defense technique of his opponent.
Little did the wolf know that this move had been exactly what Jason had wanted to see.
Amongst the icicles and fireballs, there were unique blazing icicles whose tip was extremely sharp and thick.
Ordering the flames inside some of the icicles to explode the moment the lightning hit them, he saw the heavy tip shatter into thousands of shards, distracting the lightning wolf.
This happened to owe to the lightning bolts that were attacking every single ice shard that flew through the air.
Taking advantage of its distraction, Jason appeared in front of the wolf only a moment later, looking up to it before he slashed out at its front legs.
Brandishing the weapon horizontally, he planned to pack a punch with his slash, which was created by using Solaris' flames.
At the same time, Jason enlarged Byakur at the last possible moment, creating an unforeseen situation, which the wolf had to face.
Occupied with deflecting the countless ice shards, the majority of lightning currents were currently shooting out towards the top, leaving the wolf's lower body unguarded.
Despite that, the wolf's reflexes were fast enough to notice Jason, making it flap its wings before it would be too late.
Unfortunately, Jason had already taken this possibility into consideration.
As such, his horizontal slash was altered as he jumped towards the wolf, ignoring the lightning currents that burned through his scaled armor.
Searing through the wolf's chest, Solaris' flames charred its fur, only for a fraction of its essence to enter the wolf's body.
The moment it realised this, blood had already begun to splurt out of the large wound.
Nonetheless, the severe injury it had sustained only enraged the winged two-headed lightning wolf that shot forward with the entire mana that was left in one of the two mana cores.
The mana was more than enough to flood the surrounding three meters with lightning currents that hit every single scale on his body to no avail.
Gritting his teeth, Jason was glad that Petri's scales were much more powerful than he could have expected, which was extremely beneficial for every kind of situation.
They seemed to have an elemental resistance too, which he had never noticed, otherwise, the scales of a Pryr beast at the 9th Lique stage would have never been strong enough to overcome the attack of a Low 1st threshold Prismar stage beast.
Nevertheless, the elemental resistance was not perfect. That would be too advantageous, and fortunate on his side, allowing him to become omnipotent.
Despite not being omnipotent, by fusing both Jason and Petri's capabilities were enhanced which meant that every single body part that Petri manifested had the combined strength of both fused individuals, namely him and his soulbond.
This included the strength of even the smallest capability which was the sole reason for Jason to be alive, as the race specific weakening curse had been enhanced to a much higher degree than usual.
This was the essential difference between a common body part manifestation that was possible with a simple fortified soul conjunction and a true fusion of two beings.
With his scale armor being burned, Jason had to give his utmost efforts to leave the wolf's range, escaping the range of the lightning currents.
Only then was he finally able to take a deep breath before a faint smile emerged on his face.
His scales might have been burned, but that was not an injury worth mentioning.
Instead, the wolf's injury was much worse because it was a severe wound that worsened owing to Solaris' essence flame that was burning the wolf from the inside.
It took some time, but Jason was able to evade the wolf, whose speed was slowing down with time.
As such, once Solaris had devoured the wolf's lifeforce, while burning it from the inside, it succumbed to its injuries, leaving the severely burned Jason behind.
However, just a moment before the wolf died, Jason's charred scales fell to the ground, revealing his unscathed skin.
**
After facing the winged two-headed lightning wolf, Jason had become more careful about the opponents he had to face.
Luckily, he didn't have to face another beast, which allowed him to finish the first trial in merely half the given time.
This was mostly owing to the fact that he had burned the forest, while simultaneously avoiding the strongest beasts inside it.
It hadn't been necessary because the mutated wolf had been the strongest beast of the entire forest. It wasn't fearsome owing to its sole strength, but the extraordinarily strong and unique ability to fuse with its brethren was what made it a powerful opponent.
Because of that, Jason was glad that there hadn't been more beasts with a mutation, even less, a dangerous one like the winged lightning wolf had.

chapters.title: Chapter 702 - Infinite Maze
chapters.content:
Jason was not sure if the Preactors had to finish the same Trials as him, but he assumed that they would pass them much more quickly than him.
That would, at least, make some sense owing to the fact that they had been so confident in their own capabilities.
Nevertheless, Jason was not sure how advantageous it would be if the three Preactors would be faster or slower than him.
As such, he could only continue advancing through the trials.
After Jason passed the first trial, the immediate surroundings around him twisted and he was teleported somewhere else as the familiar robotic voice resounded in his head.
[First trial successfully completed. Required time [36H:42M:04S]! Good achievement.
All beasts inside the dome have been defeated. Excellent achievement.]
[Merit points according to efficiency and speed have been added to merit bank.]
[Second Trial starts. Pass through the Infinite Maze. Allotted time [30 Days]]
When Jason appeared in the area where the second trial was held, he saw nothing but grey stone walls.
Standing in the center of a place with more than ten paths that led to different directions, Jason turned in all of the directions, trying to make sense of what was going on.
'I'm in the middle of a maze? That's great!!' He thought, with a bright smile one his face.
Making use of his Emperor Eyes, Jason was able to see a rough blueprint of the Maze consisting of the stone walls in a radius of more than 50 meters around him.
This was owing to the difference between energy fluctuations released by materials in comparison to the freely moving cultivation energies.
Jason found this to be useful enough, but owing to his Emperor Eyes, he could clearly see all kinds of traps that had been placed inside the Maze.
At the same time, there were beasts roaming in the Maze, increasing the difficulty to venture through it even more.
Nevertheless, Jason was not worried because the beasts' strength didn't seem to be high enough to kill him in the blink of an eye.
As such, he couldn't help but feel his confidence increasing.
'I can definitely be faster than everyone else in this trial!!'
With the advantage he had received, Jason wanted to charge up to Jennifer as quickly as possible.
In his opinion, this would be the best because his gut feeling told him so.
The preactors wrathful hue worried Jason.
And even without their unique hue, their combined strength, and what they had been saying to each other before entering the Inheritance site, was definitely worrisome.
However, at the same time, the fact that the Preactors came from far away, just to retrieve something, spoke volumes about the value of the things they were supposed to take back.
Because of that, Jason believed that Jennifer should definitely try to obtain said item, even if it meant that she would have to fight against the four Preactors!
Unfortunately, without additional help, Jennifer would die in that fight, which was the reason Jason wanted to inform her about everything.
Maybe, she would attempt to assassinate them, and defeat an opponent before they could even react.
In the end, this was just something Jason imagined.
It was unlikely that the Preactors would get assassinated so easily.
They held themselves in high regard as they were considered to be prodigies of their race, which meant that they had some treasures that would protect their lives if their reflexes were too slow.
With that in mind, passing the Inheritance trial as quickly as possible before leaving the Preactors behind would probably be the best.
Unfortunately, Jason felt that this was not as easy as it sounded.
Nevertheless, he could and would try his best as always!
Now that his mind had been set in stone, Jason chose one of the many paths before he began to rush through the vast space that had nothing but walls, traps, and beasts.
At the same time, he marked every path he took, trying to create a rough understanding of the maze in order to leave as quickly as possible.
Once he found a dead-end, Jason would simply leave a different symbol to mark the path at the last intersection.
Simultaneously, he would always take the left path in order to know where he had been and where he had yet to go.
This would make everything much easier, and it should allow him to rush through the Maze without any delay.
In the end, he was even able to find out whether some paths were dead-ends before he even entered them, owing to the Emperor Eyes that were currently utilised with a vast, yet, replenishable amount of mana.
Thus, adding the other factors, Jason was able to advance through the Maze without any delay.
Despite running through it for several days, he didn't feel bored at all.
There were all kinds of things he had to pay attention to and thus he was always alert.
Yet, he could simply bypass all kinds of traps that had been laid out. Because of that, his advancement speed was terrifyingly high.
He felt that the maze was perfectly suitable for him, which meant that he was likely to pass it with lots of time on hand.
Unfortunately, that was not exactly useful because he didn't really need to gain the approval of the inheritance site in order to receive the main reward.
This was simply not needed because he didn't have three cultivation veins to make use of the possible reward, to begin with.
Nevertheless, Jason could also hand over whatever he might be rewarded with to Jennifer, if she required it.
Nonetheless, he had yet to receive anything, and Jason hadn't even completed the maze either.
As such, he should first pass all trials before doing other stupid things.
Unfortunately, it was only ten days after the second trial had started that Jason noticed something odd.
He had already passed by many large intersections with constructions in them.
Within these structures, he found all kinds of things, which Jason simply picked on a whim, not minding what exactly they were.
It didn't look any special, but according to his understanding of Inheritance sites, these may contain clues to help him pass the trials.
Because of that, he studied the things he had picked up from the structures.
There were photographs, books, and all kinds of objects, but nothing seemed to be extremely helpful.
Only the seemingly logical fact that the maze was infinite just as the trial had said.
Initially, Jason had believed that this statement was an exaggeration, but that didn't seem to be the case at all.
Instead, it was probably exactly as the trial said, just that the word 'infinite' was misused.
In the end, there had been all kinds of clues showing him something Jason had to pay attention to.
However, it was only until he figured out that he had misunderstood the entire situation.
There were specific things one couldn't control in the Infinite maze, and one of those was the fact that everything looked the same adding to the confusion.
The only difference was the buildings and structures that had slight dissimilarities making them look almost identical.
And this was exactly what had allowed Jason to realise what had been wrong because he compared the items he had picked up inside all the constructions
"All items are the same... is the maze resetting itself?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 703 - Pass
chapters.content:
"All items are the same... is the maze resetting itself?!"
Jason was not sure if his assumption was correct, but if the maze was resetting itself, he would only go around in circles, there wouldn't be an end.
Even years could pass without him passing the trials.
As such, the second trial was not only designed to test one's ability to survive inside the maze, but also rational thinking, as well as the ability to tell glamour apart from reality.
It made one look at all kinds of things in detail, questioning if what was in front of them was real or an illusion.
This impressed Jason, but at the same time, he was annoyed because he had wasted too much time.
Yet, one could say that he had figured out everything much faster than others would probably be able to.
However, that did little to ease his mind because he now had to figure out how to pass the Infinite maze trial.
'If it's always resetting itself, there shouldn't be a destination I can reach just like that.
Rather, it's probably more like I have to fulfill certain requirements for something to change.
Either, the final destination is a physical place or just a portal...if it's the latter, the portal I'm looking for should be manifested through runes, in some way.
So...should I start looking for specific runes now?'
Jason tried to make up his mind, before acting.
Even if he had wasted some time, his Emperor Eyes would help him catch up soon.
That was because he didn't have to search for any clues to pass the trials but specific runes that could create portals.
His confidence grew a little because Jason had seen countless runes thousands of times during the last few months while reading many books stored in his spatial ring.
World bridges interested him the most, which was partially the case because he had yet to take revenge on certain individuals of races that had made his life miserable!
The coordinates of the planets they came from were imprinted on his mind, and even if it might just be an intermediate stop, Jason knew that he could easily find out more information in those places.
However, in order to achieve this, he required more strength.
Reaching the Specta stage would already be a great achievement because Jason assumed that the strongest beings of common races like the Ifrytor race would probably have at least one powerhouse at that stage.
As for higher races, they would have more powerhouses at that stage.
Yet, Jason was not sure how the numbers of powerhouses were at a higher stage, but it would simply take too long for most common and higher races to reach the stage after the Specta stage.
Nevertheless, the My?ldra and Burane race were strong, and Jason knew that his revenge required lots of patience and extreme strength!
Thus, it was even more important to finish the trials with the best possible result, even if the final inheritance was not suitable to him.
Other rewards were still great enough to make him work even harder, while he also had other tasks to complete.
With that in mind, Jason began examining all runes he could find with a distinct look in his eyes.
Because there were thousands of runes, and he had to pay attention to each of them, it took Jason more than three days before the Infinite maze seemed to reset once again.
However, in the meantime, Jason had found the answer to what he had been looking for.
'Each trap is connected to? the other, and the building construction has one particular rune which activates a portal with the energy supplied by the traps?' He asked himself, not sure if that made sense.
Triggering traps would lose all of the mana that had been used to empower them.
As such, if neither he nor any other beast would trigger even a single trap, the supply of energy would be more than enough to activate the rune inside the building construction.
That had to be the case, otherwise, Jason was not sure why every single trap would be connected to the unique-looking house.
Thus, he rushed towards it, the moment the Infinite maze reset, without triggering even a single trap before he activated the well-hidden rune. Somehow, it was as easy as that, which caused Jason to wonder whether he had just wasted his time, or if everything was different than it seemed.
But that didn't seem to be the case because every single trace of energy gathered inside the house, only to fully activate the rune.
Through this, the traps were now void of energy while a small blue shining portal appeared in front of Jason.
He was not sure how others were supposed to find the rune inside the small house, let alone find out that every single trap was connected to it, providing the necessary energy to create the portal.
However, that was not his problem, rather, it was his fortune because it was clear that the others would take longer to finish the same trial.
With that in mind, he leaped through the portal, entering the third trial without any hesitation.
[Second trial successfully passed. Time required [14D:2H:15M:59S]. Extraordinary achievement!
150% necessary energy supplied/No trap triggered. Excellent achievement!]
[Merit points according to efficiency and speed have been added to merit bank]
Hearing the voice inside his head, Jason didn't even feel uncomfortable anymore.
Instead, he grew accustomed to it, listening to everything intently, while eagerly awaiting the next message about the third trial.
Yet, he was surprised to receive the next message.
[Third trial will start soon. Teleportation towards the gathering point was delayed due to unforeseen circumstances in the trials of other participants!]
Jason was not pleased to hear this. Instead, he couldn't help but feel a little bit worried.
From the looks of it, the Preactors had either done something they shouldn't, without caring about the aftermath, or they had passed specific trials by unfair means.
The trials were supposed to test someone according to their suitability to specific inheritances.
However, at the same time, most inheritances were simply testing the overall capabilities of certain individuals, and as long as they crossed the threshold, they passed.
Jason didn't know the exact requirements, but he knew that passing the trials with a better score was logically considered to be better than passing it by narrowly crossing the threshold.
As such, it might even be better to do their best if one wanted to receive the final inheritance.
However, this was exactly what confused Jason because the Preactors were obviously trying to retrieve what seemed to have been taken away from them.
As such, they were likely to try to pass the trials with the highest possible score.
In the end, Jason didn't know what had caused the delay, and he could only wait.
He was not sure how much time had passed, but it didn't feel long as he received another notification into his mind as the robotic voice rang through his head.
[Third trial has started. Demonstrate your talent and unique features within the following hours. After everything is shown, the third trial will be concluded!]
Jason was not sure what exactly he had expected for the third trial, but he hadn't expected to hear something so vague.
As such, he couldn't help but feel a little bit astonished as he summarised the requirements to pass the trials until now.
'First combat strength, and survivability, then logical thinking, and perception, and now talent and trust to reveal my secrets? What else will this inheritance test me...my honesty or what?!'

chapters.title: Chapter 704 - Superior
chapters.content:
Jason felt uncomfortable with the choice of words the robotic voice had used to announce the third trial's task.
'After everything is shown' implied that he had to reveal all of his hidden traits, which was definitely not what he wanted, even to pass the trial.
However, this was only a small issue in face of the multitude of hand-sized spheres that were levitating inside the room he had been teleported to.
The three orbs in the center stood out from the rest and one of them looked eerily familiar to Jason.
"Mana mastery orb!" he blurted out only to realise what the orbs right next to it were.
'Don't tell me I need to insert spirit force and primordial energy into the orbs to let my mastery in those two cultivation veins be tested?'
With 'everything is shown' it was given that he had to reveal his talent in all three cultivation paths because to enter the Inheritance site, he was required to have all three veins.
However, in his case, this had been different because Jason was able to enter the Inheritance site just because of his heritage, or at least that was what he understood based on the first messages he had received from the robotic voice.
There were all kinds of other things he had to pay attention to right now, but revealing all of his secrets wouldn't be a child's play in comparison to showing something he didn't even possess!
For a short moment, Jason felt desperate, asking himself how he was supposed to leave the Inheritance site if he could not even pass the third trial.
There was also no countdown which meant that he wouldn't be thrown out if he failed the trial because there was no indicator of what a failure in this trial even was!
This was bad, to put it simply, and Jason couldn't help but acknowledge that he felt a little bit anxious.
However, just a moment later, the thought of Spyro and Petri came into his mind, which made him smile lightly.
Wasting no time, he quickly summoned his soulbonds who looked at him in confusion before Jason explained the entire situation neatly.
Afterward, Jason approached the orbs, whose content was clearly visible to him due to his Emperor Eyes.
Sharing his sight with both, he enabled them to see everything about their own mastery orb clearly.
Through this, they could think of an approach to pass their mastery orb, and Jason did the same.
That was important because the mastery orb in front of him was extremely difficult to solve owing to the countless knots it had.
He had never seen something as complex if he were to exclude world bridges. As such, he realised that he had to pay more attention to passing the test.
That was, even more, the case because Jason couldn't rely on Petri, let alone Spyro to pass the test, even if they had enough time.
Because of that, Jason was the first to begin, showing his soulbonds how it had to be done as he shared every single experience and detail he perceived and saw!
In the end, it took him more than two hours to finish the test, and it was only then that he noticed that both his soulbonds had already started with their own mastery test.
A few more hours passed in which Jason continued to share the inside of both orbs while guiding Spyro, who was struggling the most.
It was a newborn Spirit, after all, and Jason couldn't simply expect it to be perfect from the day it was born.
As such, once all three mastery tests were completed, he was not astonished about Spyro's Spirit mastery result.
[Mana mastery- Superior; passed!]
[Spirit mastery- average; failed!]
[Primordial energy mastery- above-average - passed!]
Both of his soulbonds had still not matured and were growing. This meant that their control over Spirit force and Primordial energy was still improving.
He might have failed one test, but even if that was already enough to make him fail everything, he would have at least found a way out of the third trial!
Nevertheless, the fact that Petri passed the test was already shocking to Jason because the Basilisk had perfectly employed the information he had been provided with.
As such, it had been possible for Petri to reach an above-average mastery in an extremely difficult test.
In the end, the three tests had evaluated the time required to fully untie the knots of intertwined strands of energy.
With that in mind, Petri might have finished the task barely sometime before he reached the maximum time limit, but that did not matter, having passed the test was the essential point!
Even Jason couldn't help but feel that it was tens of times more difficult than the most difficult mana mastery orb he had solved.
However, that was not exactly impossible to happen because the last time he had tested his mana mastery was on Argos at the liberation tournament!
As such, it was surprising that he received a Superior mana mastery at a test that was supposed to be extremely difficult to pass.
In the end, it would be frustrating to leave the Inheritance site right now without having met and reported everything to Jennifer. But, the worst-case scenario at least gave him the opportunity to leave, which was better than being imprisoned forever!
Because of that, he couldn't complain as he continued to reveal his Celestia aura and Stigma, unleashing them to the fullest extent.
Following that, he used the curses and his abyssal ability, only to add their combined force.
Even after doing all of the above the third trial was still requesting him to reveal more.
This was annoying, thus Jason simply revealed all his remaining capabilities.
Fusing with Petri, he simultaneously summoned Solaris, and Byakur, only to release his entire mana that was not only much stronger than others but also four times more in quantity.
Yet, despite having shown everything, the trial was still not done and the robotic voice didn't resound in his mind.
Thus, he summoned Artemis, who was in her cocoon, followed by his entire soul world which he manifested inside the space around him.
Right now, he just wanted to pass the exam and leave.
As such, he revealed his soul world that had reached a size Jason didn't even know.
Jason only knew that it was gigantic, and still growing, which was why he had never bothered about figuring out the exact size.
Its size had never mattered to him, after all!
After the soul world had been summoned, the entire space around him twisted, because the small dome he was in was too small to accommodate the soul world in its entirety.
Because of that, Jason had to retract it a moment later, followed by allowing his soulbonds to leave with the soul world, where they returned to.
However, even after all of this, the trial was still not completed, which made him angry and confused at the same time.
"What else is there for me to show? It's not like I concealed anything...My eyes, the soul world, my soulbonds, the Celestia aura, all Stimas, my highly compressed prismarine crystal, the curses, what else is unique about me?!"
Utterly confused, Jason required almost a whole hour before he realised that he had forgotten something he had learned a long time ago.
'Don't tell me it's the pressure I comprehended??'
This shouldn't be the case, but Jason nonetheless released his pressure without using a single mana particle.
Yet, this didn't seem to be the right answer, only to give Jason a hint that caused him to frown.
"It cannot be the chaos attribute, or the soul fraction of the mysterious beast, right? The chaos attribute shouldn't be counted as my unique feature…."

chapters.title: Chapter 705 - Back Together
chapters.content:
I don't believe that it really was the chaos attribute that I had to reveal...how the hell is that supposed to be my own trait?!
After revealing the chaos attribute, Jason had exposed every single secret, or at least the Inheritance site accepted that he did so.
As such, he was once again enveloped in white light as the space around him twisted.
Only a moment later, the already familiar robotic voice returned.
[3rd trial has been completed successfully. The number of unique traits exceeded the highest threshold. Congratulations; Superior achievement attained!]
[Teleportation to the 4th, and second last trial, has been initiated.]
[Fourth trial; Endure the ever-increasing pressure until you lose consciousness!]
The message of the fourth trial astonished Jason a lot because he didn't expect the trial to have anything to do with Pressure.
'Pressure again? Why are so many trials even focusing on this?...it's not like I can use it well in order to fight stronger opponents... But this time it probably includes all three energies releasing pressure…could this be a technique handed out to those that pass the trials as a reward?'
This would make sense, but at the same time, it was not worth being the main Inheritance. At least, Jason was pretty sure that a technique on how to release pressure was worth being the most valuable reward in an Inheritance site, yet not the main inheritance!
For the main reward in an inheritance, there were only a few things worth enough to be mentioned, including the forceful alteration of one's body structure!
As such, those Inheritances were one-of-a-kind, or at least very close to that!
However, in the end, none of that should be an issue for Jason, because his Celestia aura and Emperor Eyes were proficient in dispersing pressure around him as long as he wanted that to happen!
He was not sure how well this would work for all three energies, but he was not worried about it at all.
Yet, what made him feel a little bit iffy was the fact that the Fourth trial would only end when one lost consciousness.
With that in mind, Jason couldn't help but feel that something bad was about to happen.? His eyes fell on Jennifer's silhouette further away from him, the moment he appeared at the location where the fourth trial was held.
No sooner had he appeared, the pressure of three intertwined energies enveloped Jason, forcing him to his knees before he could even react.
His muscles groaned and his joints creaked, and it was only when Jason was finally able to release the Celestia aura, followed by inserting mana into the Emperor Eyes that the pressure dispersed.
He knew that this was only a temporary solution, but it would definitely help him stay conscious for more than a week.
That should be enough to pass and enter the last trial.
Yet, this was not why he had entered the Inheritance site of the three energies, to begin with.
His reason had been Jennifer and given that she was endangered due to the sudden appearance of the Preactors.
As such, he had to report everything to her. He knew he wouldn't be a match for their strength but he at least hoped to stay by her side and possibly help her figure out how they could defeat the Preactors.
What he lacked in muscle he made up with strategic thinking so he hoped he could find a way out without being heavily injured, let alone dying in the same attempt.
Because of that, Jason got up from the ground, only to notice that the pressure on him was not completely dispersed.
However, it was not high enough to make him feel like he was suffocating.
Thus, he didn't bother to insert more mana into his Emperor Eyes.
Instead, Jason quickly approached Jennifer, who was fully concentrated while trying to endure and simultaneously comprehend the three merged pressures that filled the area around her.
Jason felt that the pressure in Jennifer's immediate surroundings was extremely strong, which was a bad sign, considering that she was likely to be facing four opponents that had similar combat prowess to her, soon.
The moment Jason appeared around Jennifer, her silver eyes opened instinctively as her reflexes took over.
Within an instant, her fingers curled around the two daggers in her hand, as she got up from the ground.
She released all three of her energies and disappeared from his sight.
A quarter of a second later, Jason felt a cold blade graze his neck as he heard a question.
"Who are you, and why are you taking on the appearance of my friend!?"
At first, Jason didn't understand what Jennifer was doing.
However, after a few seconds, he realised that she didn't believe that he could enter the Inheritance site owing to its requirement, which was logical.
Yet, it made the current situation a little bit more difficult to solve.
As such, he tried to speak, which was hardly possible owing to the blade that cut into his neck, causing a few droplets of blood to trickle down.
"Jen….mana fluctuations…"
Not being able to say anymore, Jason hoped that Jen would at least stop exerting pressure on the blade she held against his neck. Jason knew it pretty well that the strength she used was not something he could easily endure, let alone block.
He might have advanced to the Prismar stage, but he had a long way to go to reach her strength!
Hearing Jason's voice and his words, she couldn't help but look at his mana fluctuations.
However, that made her only more suspicious because Jason's mana fluctuations were truly exactly the same as she recalled.
Despite that, he shouldn't have been able to enter the Inheritance site, to begin with!
Yet, somehow, she felt that it was odd, and she retracted her dagger a little bit as she asked.
"If you are really Jason, how did you even enter the Inheritance site? This was impossible for you earlier!!"
Jason had expected her to ask a different question that only he could know the answer to in order to verify his identity, but that was not what Jennifer asked.
Because of that, Jason didn't answer for a moment only to blurt out, "After advancing to the Prismar stage, the Celestia aura swept through the temple and I felt the same suction force you felt. However, that was not enough reason for me to enter the temple inheritance because I don't have the innate talent of possessing three cultivation veins.
As such, I had planned to leave and search for my own inheritance, until four Preactors arrived, entering temple owing to their three cultivation energies!"
Being able to speak properly once again, Jason made proper use of this opportunity, giving her a brief summary that caused Jennifer to halt in her tracks.
'Celestia aura? Preactors….three cultivation energies?'
In the end, Jennifer was utterly confused, but it was only now that she sensed his aura once again, and a moment later, Jennifer's eyes locked with Jason's as he turned his head towards her.
They were glowing in the overly familiar colors, and deep within them, Jennifer could detect kindness and all other emotions that had been hidden in the depth of his soul.
In her entire life, she had only come across a few people in her life whose eyes were the entrance to their soul, hiding or revealing certain emotions, and Jason was one of those few.
Adding his dense mana fluctuations, the unique aura he released, and the golden glow, she couldn't believe that he was not an illusion, let alone someone from a different race trying to mimic his appearance and every single characteristic. No matter how proficient one was, it was simply not possible to do something like this to near perfection.
As such, Jennifer completely retracted her daggers, giving Jason some space to breathe, only to hear him complain.
"Do I have to endure something like that every single time, I want to save you from a miserable death?!"
Jason's complaint confused her, but at the same time, she recalled what he had said earlier.
"What did you mean with the Celestia aura? That's not your aura, right? And who or what exactly are the Preactors? Did you see them, and how are you so sure that they will pass all the trials up to the fourth? The first three trials were already difficult, and I almost didn't make it out of the maze!"
Listening to her, he couldn't help but feel confused because she didn't even wonder how he had passed the trials while saying that the others wouldn't pass them easily.
Either she didn't notice that he had passed the same trials, or took him to be much stronger than he had believed Jennifer would.
In the end, this was not the important factor, and he also ignored the question about his aura, as he explained everything he had noticed about the Preactors.
This took him less than 10 minutes, and when he was done, Jennifer looked at him in doubt.
"So...you want to tell me that four Preactors at the peak Prismar stage, with three awakened cultivation veins, entered the Inheritance site that was created by one of their traitors, who stole something.
Other than that, it was just their punishment which forced them to obey their superior, who sent them to the Inheritance site to take their treasures back to their home planet that is also much better than Manyr?
...That sounds...very unique…"
Jennifer didn't even question whether he was stating the truth or not, and simply accepted everything Jason had said.
"Yes, and they're extremely dangerous because they seem to be filled with wrath, and act impulsive, otherwise, they wouldn't have attacked and killed prodigies at a gathering event….
That is under the assumption that what I heard was true!"
Jason felt like adding this because it was the major reason for him to follow Jennifer into the Inheritance site.
He didn't want her to be injured, let alone die because of the Preactors.
As such, he had planned to finish the trials and leave them as quickly as possible.
However, from the looks of it, the fourth trial was shattering his plan because they were unable to leave without losing their consciousness.
At that moment, Jennifer smiled schemingly as she said,
"If that's the case, let's kick their butts. If we cannot kill them, let's force them to lose their consciousness the moment they arrive...that is, if they're really as confident as you said!!"

chapters.title: Chapter 706 - Seals
chapters.content:
Jennifer's confidence caused Jason to look at her in doubt.
Even though she was strong, they were talking about knocking out four beings that originated from an even greater planet, with roughly the same combat prowess as Jennifer!
That was not something they could do just because Jennifer deemed it easy, and Jason couldn't help but think that she was underestimating the threat.
However, her next words were not something Jason expected to hear.
"If you use your chaos attribute just like last time, you should be able to release a similar effect as you did with Prince Leo, right?
Considering that you are much stronger now, even I shouldn't be unfazed by the combined attack of your curses, the abyssal effect you told me about, and the chaos attribute!"
These words caused Jason to stiffen because he didn't expect that Jennifer was seriously considering his participation in this fray.
However, that was not all because it looked like she wanted to gamble on him and see whether he would be able to achieve the same feat as before.
Seeing the dumbfounded look on his face, Jennifer couldn't help but smile weirdly as she asked,
"Can you not do that?"
She didn't sound mad or annoyed at all.
It was more like Jennifer knew that the chaos attribute was not exactly his own, just a weird additional trait that he had within him, and could control it to a certain extent.
Because of that, she had secretly hoped that Jason could do the same feat over and over again, as long as he met certain requirements.
Yet, from the look on his face, it seemed to be a little bit more complicated.
This caused her to feel that executing her earlier plan was more difficult than expected. Thus she had already begun to think of other solutions to stay inside the Inheritance site without being killed or losing on the merit points she had accumulated.
However, it was not necessary to completely scrap her earlier plan because Jennifer's idea had been decent!
"I can use the chaos attribute, but I'm not exactly sure whether or not this will be enough. I don't feel as angry or emotionally affected as I was feeling at that time…"
It was already a good sign that Jason was confident to use the chaos attribute once again, but the second half of his line pertaining to his emotions was rather disadvantageous.
Not knowing how strong his attack truly was, it could either be enough or a complete disaster.
This uncertainty was not good, but Jennifer thought that it was better than nothing.
As such, she would be the last one to complain, owing to the fact that she was the reason Jason even entered the Inheritance site.
Despite him being evidently weaker than the four Preactors, he wanted to help.
This seemingly simple gesture made Jennifer feel warm in her heart which made her smile vibrantly.
Jason, who didn't realise what Jennifer was thinking about, could only look at her in doubt, wondering what made her smile in a tricky situation like the one they were in.
Thinking about his own capabilities, Jason realised that there were many minor seals he could destroy.
Before, his cultivation speed had been too slow to even consider breaking one minor seal without possibly endangering him.
However, that wasn't the case anymore.
Rather than cultivating too slowly, the number of seals on him seemed to be too much. What this meant was that Jason had never truly thought that he would be able to increase his cultivation speed to the extent that allowed him to break multiple seals at once.
But that was now happening, and the thought that he would never be able to break all seals that were put on his bloodline disappeared too!
Yet, it was exactly this that caused Jason to feel that the Celestia bloodline was even more dangerous to a human halfling like him than he had initially thought.
There were thousands of minor seals on his body, some were bigger, some smaller, and Jason could faintly tell that those that were deeper within his bloodline were stronger.
However, right now, he had only destroyed a few of them.
This hadn't bothered him before because he had never put much thought on the seals, but after clearly inspecting the helix in the depths of his conscience, Jason felt that Luna's reaction about his revelation of being a Celestia was suitable.
'Every single seal I release will strengthen my Celestia aura, the Stigma, possibly even my soul world, my sensitivity towards mana, and much more!' Jason realised. His mind subconsciously began pondering over the question of who the mysterious being that had sealed his bloodline truly was.
The being, whose soul fraction was imprinted into his mind, had to be an existence whose power is either on par with the Celestias, or its power was simply perfectly suitable to seal Jason's bloodline.
In the end, the answer remained hidden, and Jason's mind returned to the more important question.
"How many seals can I break, and how long will I be able to lock the four Preactors in their place, giving Jennifer the necessary time to act?"
Jason voiced out his concern loudly without noticing. This caused Jennifer to look at him in confusion.
Yet, before she could even say something, Jason averted his gaze, locking his eyes with her as he asked,
"If they cannot move, how much time do you need to knock them out?"
Jason didn't even try to think about killing them because they were likely to have automatic protective mechanisms, like specific medallions that would protect them if they were about to die.
As such, knocking them out would be the easiest way to force them outside the Inheritance trials.
Afterward, the Preactors might wait outside the temple in order to ambush them, but during that time Jennifer could receive the inheritance, and become much stronger that would help her in defeating the four Preactors.
At least, that was the plan Jason had put together within a few moments.
There was nothing special about his plan, but he felt that it was the most suitable.
"If they're rendered incapable of defending themselves, let alone move from their place, I need two seconds, at most three, and that is already the maximum!!"
Jennifer answered reluctantly, not sure if she was demanding too much, but seeing Jason simply nod his head made her worries disperse in thin air.
"I don't know if I can shackle them down for three seconds, but two seconds are feasible!
They won't be able to budge, so kick their butts and knock them out once they arrive."
In the end, neither Jason nor Jennifer were sure if the four Preactors would arrive at the exact same time or the same location, or if all of them would even make it through the first few trials!
Jason didn't think that they would face all the trials in a group, but the possibility was still there.
As such, enduring the pressure around them, both Jennifer and Jason created multiple plans.
Several days passed, and they had already started to focus on their other task, which was to endure the pressure.
At the same time, Jason was cultivating, trying to make use of the extremely dense, pure, and high quantity of mana around him.
If he wanted to be on par with Jennifer, he was required to cultivate more, longer, and faster than she was doing.
His cultivation speed might be faster than hers, but Jennifer would soon undergo her first bloodline awakening, of both bloodlines, at the same time.
If she were to overcome this painful experience, her strength would skyrocket, and reach a level that was similar to her cultivation speed.
As such, Jason wanted to reduce the gap between his strength and hers as much as possible before Jennifer advanced to the Ascension stage.
He was also not sure what kind of Aeus and Devir her parents were, but according to her cultivation speed, they had been extremely talented.
This made him wonder what exactly Jennifer's story was because she seemed to hate both the Aeus and Devir race equally which was weird.
'Just what happened to you, Jennifer?'
