chapters.title: Chapter 727 - 10th Floor
chapters.content:
With the new information in hand, Jason used the next three days to clear the beasts from the second floor before he spent an entire week cultivating.
This was not enough to construct the second solidified prismarine crystal, and it would take at least three more weeks of fully focused cultivation.
Because of that, Jason advanced to the third and fourth floor, killing all beasts first before doing the same to the guardians.
Afterward, he would only enter the next floor, just before he would stop receiving the speed bonus.
Through this, Jason could cultivate while receiving all possible bonuses, which was exactly what he wanted.
In the end, entering the fifth floor took him an entire month, but it was definitely worth it because the second solidified prismarine crystal was finally created!
With that, Jason's combat prowess almost doubled in an instant, and he knew that he could further increase the speed at which he enhanced.
However, that was only something Jason realised after advancing to the fifth floor.
The increase in difficulty he had expected turned out to be minuscule, and it was mostly the Guardian that had become stronger.
Yet, Jason's increase in strength was much higher than that of the Guardian's because not only his own strength had been enhanced, but that of his soulbonds received a boost too.
Spyro's spirit veins had fully recuperated, and owing to the enormous amount of spirit force and the spiral cricula Minatra flowers that had been planted inside his soul world, it had already reached the 8th Lique stage.
Meanwhile, Petri was relentlessly absorbing primordial energy in order to liquefy and solidify it afterward.
Artemis would still need some time to evolve, but Jason was already awaiting it eagerly.
He assumed that his soul energy and the number of soul crystals he would have accumulated until then would be enough.
As such, they would be able to advance through the tower at a much faster pace after her evolution was completed.
Jason could wait for her to finish evolving while cultivating, but that wouldn't be interesting because the opponents from the 5th to the 9th floor were not really a threat.
In a single month, Jason had cleared these five floors, only to realise that he had been too excited to fight again. Thus, he had forgotten to focus on cultivating in the time he had in hand before the speed bonus would have worn off.
Nevertheless, Jason couldn't complain.
From the fifth floor onwards, the base reward increased to 1.5 merit points, which meant that he received a total of 4.5 Merit points for every floor he cleared.
This was exceptional, but before Jason realised it, he was already standing in front of the gate that had faint silver engravings all around it.
Yet, at the same time, there was something that bothered him a little bit.
Before, there were no clues about the next floor's dangers, but now there was the skull of a human-like being engraved in the center of the gate.
If that was not a warning, Jason was not sure what else he was supposed to think.
As such, he realised that he had to pay attention to what he was doing on the 10th floor.
However, instead of being frightened, Jason realised that the dangers of the tower had gradually decreased with each subsequent floor.
That was not how it was ought to be according to the danger level which the artificial intelligence had assigned beforehand.
Not only was he facing the highest difficulty level of the entire dungeon, but, in fact, the dungeon had created a new difficulty level just for him.
Because of that, Jason had been worried beforehand, only to overcome the basement level and the first nine floors of the tower without any real issues.
In the end, he had spent more than two months inside the dungeon, yet, it felt as if he had just entered it.
At the same time, he was yet to witness the overwhelming strength of his opponents that the artificial intelligence had mentioned.
Instead, the common beasts he faced were weaker than him, while the Guardian had barely been on par with his prowess.
And that was before he solidified his second prismarine crystal!
As such, the skull on the 10th floor should either be an exaggeration or a symbol of true dangers, which was the way Jason perceived it.
It should be dangerous, but owing to his combat prowess that exceeded the peak of the Prismar stage's first threshold, he was confident of defeating the Guardian on the 10th Floor.
And even if he was too weak to defeat the Guardian, the common beasts shouldn't be strong enough to survive his onslaught.
His combat prowess was too high, after all!
It was unlikely that the common beasts had reached the peak of the Prismar stage's first threshold, while the possibility of them advancing to the Initial stage of the second threshold was infinitely small, but not zero.
As such, Jason couldn't help but feel his hands tremble in excitement as he entered the portal that led him to the 10th Floor.
Within no time, he emerged on a plain with blueish flourishing grass and extremely dense mana that permeated the surrounding area.
Meanwhile, the primordial energy and spiral force were much lower in comparison, which astonished Jason a little bit.
Before there had never been a difference between the amount, purity, and density of the three energies, but that seemed to have changed now!
'With that amount of mana, I wouldn't even need a single cultivation stone to reach my highest cultivation speed!' Jason thought, only to sense something from the corner of his eye.
It was only a moment later that a barrage of icicles shot towards him, almost killing him the moment he emerged out of the portal.
Fortunately, his Emperor Eyes had sensed the mana fluctuations from more than a kilometer away, giving him the required time to duck and lay flat on the ground before constructing a gigantic wall of ice himself.
The last time he used his ice affinity was quite some time ago, and he couldn't help notice that it had become much weaker than it had been before.
Yet, what Jason had to understand was that his affinities were not becoming weaker, but that his strength and the opponents he faced were becoming too strong.
Every few months, Jason could solidify one prismarine crystal that had the same potency as four common solidified crystals.
That was simply an insane feat and not something others were able to achieve under normal circumstances.
In the end, it was something that belonged to the Celestia race's innate traits, which Jason didn't know for sure.
He simply believed that all stronger races could do what he did, but that was not the case, at all!
Some had unique cultivation techniques with which they could compress and liquefy their mana to a much higher extent.
Yet, Jason didn't even require such a cultivation technique, because his bloodline was forcing him to liquefy mana to a much higher extent, while the solidification process was intertwined with the faint traces of the divine energy he used.
However, right now, this didn't matter because Jason understood that he had underestimated the 10th Floor's dangers.
That was not difficult to realise when he saw a total of more than 10 Jackals that had each eight solidified prismarine crystals within their mana core!
This astonished Jason because the jackals' strength was on par with the Guardian of the previous floor.
With that intel, Jason realised that the dangers of the 10th floor were obviously much higher, and he was eager to encounter the Guardian.
However, first, he had to defeat the jackals that had almost killed him the moment he emerged from the portal!

chapters.title: Chapter 728 - Greed
chapters.content:
A slow smile crept up his face when he saw the 10 jackals facing him. His combat prowess was further enhanced by Petri, who occupied his mana core, and his own physique was equivalent to the strength received by the reinforcement of a solidified prismarine crystal. As such, Jason was powerful enough to overwhelm the jackals without any issues.
There was not even the need for him to use his Emperor Eyes, the curses he harbored, or anything else to defeat the jackals that were astonished by Jason's strength. They had underestimated him and hadn't expected him to be stronger than they could handle.
Yet, before they could even realise what was going on, he had emerged in front of them, killing them without showing any mercy.
During the last two months alone, Jason had killed much more than a thousand beasts at the Prismar stage. Previously, he had felt some remorse after killing them, but this sensation had slowly dispersed, replaced by the thought that the beasts inside the tower would attack him even if he wouldn't, either way.
His mindset slowly adjusted to feeling anything except the determination to advance through the tower, and Jason began to understand that the numbness with which he killed was slowly taking him over.
That was bad, at least, if he didn't want to become completely numb to the sensation of killing. He didn't want to transform into a mindless killing machine.
Becoming numb to killing was one of the worst things that could happen because emotions like guilt, frustration, sadness, wrath, agony, and so on were extremely important in a fight, and even more emotions were what made him 'human'.
Without these emotions, Jason knew that he would become a ruthless executioner, without any thought or logic, which was something he wanted to avoid by all means.
Nevertheless, given the dungeon's dangers, he couldn't allow the beasts to survive as the fight against the floor's Guardian might turn out to be extremely fierce.
Owing to this, the fight against the Guardian would take longer, which would in return mean that a loud commotion would ensue, attracting the attention of other beast groups.
In the end, this meant that Jason either had to defeat the Guardian quickly or the other ferocious beasts that roamed the floor.
With that in mind, Jason started to clear the floor of every single group of beasts, which gave him a rough estimation of their overall strength that had increased tremendously.
He already assumed that the difficulty of the 10th floor would increase substantially, but to think that there would be multiple beast groups with each beast having nine solidified prismarine crystals was beyond Jason's expectations.
'If the 10th Floor already has beasts at the Peak of the Prismar stage's first threshold, won't the 20th Floor be full of beasts at the 2nd threshold?!'
That was something that bothered Jason because he knew the exact and vast difference between the first and second threshold of the Prismar stage.
In the end, the difference in terms of cultivation was only the creation of a large rotating crystal that enveloped three small prismarine crystals.
Nevertheless, the enhancements of these single rotating crystals were something Jason didn't know yet.
He knew that they required several times the mana required by a single prismarine crystal only to be constructed, but that was all he was aware of.
Others didn't compare small solidified crystals with the larger rotating crystals, because it was evident who was stronger, and that it was not even questionable.
However, these beings didn't have the advantage of a higher compressed, and unique cultivation base like Jason, giving him the ability to fight against beings that were much stronger than he was.
Thus, he had to find his match soon enough.
The 10th floor was much wider than the ones before, and it took Jason almost ten days just to find and defeat all groups of beasts.
Some fights had been easier, some more difficult because more and more beast groups had been attracted by the commotion he created, but in the end, he was still unscathed.
Nevertheless, he didn't immediately approach the gate he had found relatively early.
Instead, he used his Emperor Eyes to take a look at the color of the engravings.
On one hand, Jason wanted to receive the speed bonus, but on the other hand, he wanted to be fully prepared for the worst-case scenario.
However, if he acted like this every single time dangers loomed around him, he might as well hide like a coward and only face opponents that were weaker than him.
Reflecting on his battles so far, he realised that he had fought many stronger opponents than those that were weaker than him in terms of his cultivation base.
Yet, this didn't have much of a meaning, if he were to be honest.
His peers had never really been a huge threat to him, and he quickly bridged the gap between them after he had been able to cultivate.
There might be prodigies of high-ranked races which he didn't encounter until now, but most beings he had faced so far were much older than him.
Even Jennifer was several years older than him, and it was only a difference for beasts, who grew up while simultaneously becoming stronger.
For them, their age didn't matter, and it was more of their degree of maturity that made a difference in their strength, turning them stronger or weaker.
Afterward, it was their racial limit that prevented them from reaching certain thresholds.
This restriction didn't seem to exist in the intelligent races because they only required time, the only difference being the duration of time required to cultivate.
For some, it would take millennia to reach a certain cultivation stage, while others were faster owing to their talent, background, and opportunities.
Yet, in the end, only strength mattered, and Jason had long since realised this even before he left Argos.
Because of that, he didn't care about others' age, and was more concerned about the strength others could exhibit.
Jason also knew that the thought that had coincidentally flashed through his mind had nothing to do with his current situation...or so he thought.
With his talent, he could cultivate at a rapid speed, and his strength could increase tremendously, just in a matter of a few days as long as he and his soulbonds cultivated relentlessly!
Due to this unique situation, the dangers of the tower trial could lessen, the more he cultivated, or higher, the more he rushed through the tower.
As such, with that thought in mind, Jason was forced to use his brain to figure out the best solution in terms of earning as many merit points as possible.
Knowing their value, and given the fact that the Dungeon of the Primordial Descendant was something unique, along with the fact that he would probably never be able to enter it again, Jason had to use this one chance to the fullest.
Even if he might be unable to reach the required threshold to receive the Main inheritance, this wouldn't matter as long as he was able to use the earned merit points efficiently.
Owing to this thought, his mind was running wild, and he spent the following days cultivating as if his life depended on it!
How could Jason realise that he opted for the right choice, only to be too full of himself, and greedy because he wanted to receive the speed bonus by all means?
As such, before the entire silver engravings were replaced by a blue color, Jason approached the gate, ready to attack the emerging beast at any moment.
He had already utilised all means and rushed ahead the moment the gate opened, revealing the portal that was just manifesting, only to emerge in front of the beast that appeared a moment later.
Yet, what Jason didn't expect was that the beast seemed to be waiting for him as it stared downwards at him.
It was as if it pierced into his soul and without a moment of hesitation, it brandished a huge longsword with a terrifying speed that shocked Jason to the core.
Trying to block the attack with all his might, Jason's eyes widened in shock, realising that the beast he was facing cultivated in all the three main paths!
Merging the three cultivations' energies, its strength exceeded that of Jason's by a large margin, and it was only a moment later that a sting coursed through his soul world. The impact of the sting was so huge that it was immediately transferred to his mind as a faint crack resounded through his head.
This sound flashed through his mind and it took Jason a moment to realise what was going on as he cursed out with a single, shocking thought in his mind.
'Byakur...is breaking?!'

chapters.title: Chapter 729 - Overwhelming Opponent
chapters.content:
Jason was shocked.
Never in his life would he have imagined that the opponent he had to face had such a devastating strength.
He had failed to realise the first telltale signs of his trusted weapon, Byakur receiving its very first cracks. This was an unbelievable sight, which caused Jason to widen his eyes in shock.
Instinctively, he retracted his weapon, allowing it to return to the soul world.
This gave the one-eyed giant, the Cyclops, to continue the sword slash with an unfathomable force.
Knowing the trajectory, Jason evaded it by a hair's breadth, but before he realised it, the Cyclops landed a solid kick into the abdomen.
Flung away, Jason crashed into the ground, more than a dozen meters away from his previous position, only to continue to roll.
Gasping for air, Jason felt as if his entire body was shaking, yet, before he could even think, his body reacted instinctively.
Pushing himself up from the ground, Solaris' wings manifested on his back, and he soared into the air, giving him some time to breathe, just as the Cyclops appeared below him.
Its speed was terrifying, and Jason had barely evaded it, which was his fortune.
If it had reached him in time, he would have been in a completely different situation by now.
'Three cultivation energies and it reached the 2nd threshold? What the fuck?!' Jason thought the moment he got the time to make an evaluation of his opponent's strength.
It was devastating, and it was only a moment after his initial evaluation that he was able to calm down to some extent.
'No...it's still in the 1st threshold...and has just started to create the first of three large rotating crystals!'
This find was reassuring, but the rest was definitely not.
Byakur was only slowly recuperating within his soul world, which was one of the advantages of a Soul weapon- its regeneration ability.
Yet, before the faint cracks on it would be completely healed, at least half a day or, probably more had to pass.
That was not something Jason could afford to give Byakur to heal right now.
To put it bluntly, Jason had a marginal upper hand due to Solaris' wings that enabled him to fly around the Cyclops, however, this advantage was short-lived because the Cyclops was preparing something.
Jason had a premonition about it, and without hesitation, he manifested several hundred fire needles.
He just wanted to target the Cyclops' sole eye and render it blinding, but the moment the fire needles were shot out, Jason understood that it was useless.
Solaris might be on the way to create its third solidified prismarine crystal, but there was still a big difference between possessing the strength of three prismarine crystals and nine.
Furthermore, the Cyclops had the advantage of cultivating in all three main paths.
Thus, its strength must already be at the 2nd threshold of the Prismar stage.
With that in mind, Jason couldn't help but feel a little bit odd because the opponent on the 10th Floor shouldn't already be that strong!
It simply made no sense considering that he began ascending the floor with a single solidified prismarine crystal!
Even if he was a halfling of the Celestia and human race, that didn't mean he was able to do everything!
Right now, his chances to win a battle against the Cyclops were close to zero.
As such, Jason didn't even feel like attacking the Cyclops, to begin with.
There had to be a different way of tackling the beast, and figuring it out was what he had to do right now.
Jason was able to come up with several plans owing to the Spiral Spirit being his soulbond that enhanced his mind.
Most of them had to be discarded because they were too dangerous, but one particular plan was stuck in his mind.
'The gate is open...so I should be able to enter the 11th floor, right? If I manage to leave, I can cultivate before encountering the other guardians!'
In the end, the plan was simple, and Jason wanted to employ it without hesitation.
Yet, he also knew that his speed was too slow.
Nevertheless, with the ability to fly, Jason planned to approach the gate slowly. Thus, he released his entire mana at once while flying towards the gate carefully in an attempt to speed through the portal.
Unfortunately, his plan shattered into smithereens, the moment he realised that the Cyclops didn't remain idle.
Instead, its eyes were fixated on Jason from the beginning of the battle, but it was only now that it began to act.
Huge streams of energy enveloped the Cyclops, only to gather around its eye that began to release a unique kind of merged energy.
At this moment, Jason understood that the Cyclops was using a weird type of special technique.
Yet, before Jason could do anything, whether it was desperately attacking, or fleeing, his surroundings seemed to twist as the gravitational force increased by several times.
Unsure whether it was just his mind that assumed the gravitational force was increasing, or if the Cyclops was pulling him towards it, Jason could only stare at the Cyclops for a confused minute.
However, it was crystal clear that he wouldn't be able to continue flying anymore.
He was only a few meters away from the portal, but at the same time, this small distance suddenly became too vast to cross for him!
Looking down, he noticed that the Cyclops was merely inches away from him, and both the joy and killing intent inside its eyes caused Jason to feel that he couldn't hold back anything anymore.
Otherwise, he might die!
At that moment, Jason did something he had wanted to prevent at all costs because he could tell that his body was not ready yet!
Earlier, he had already unsealed many minor seals, and if it was possible to do that again, he would do it by all means.
However, this time it was different.
Forcefully releasing another seal, Jason grit his teeth, knowing that this seal was different compared to the ones before!
It was not a minor seal, but one of the few bigger seals the Chaos Emperor had put on him.
This seal had multiple purposes, but among the most important was the fact that the major seals of the Chaos Emperor prevented the Celestia bloodline from directly merging with and overwhelming Jason's human bloodline!
Only because of that, Jason was able to awaken the soul world, in the first place, and it was similar to his humane emotions that wouldn't have existed without the human blood coursing through his veins!
As such, the moment Jason broke his seal, the energy that was released almost tore his body apart, as the Celestia bloodline tried to suppress the human bloodline.
Yet, before anything like that could happen, the Cyclops seemed to have noticed that something was odd, which caused it to react instinctively.
Only a fraction of a second later, Jason's eyes were sprayed with hot blood- his blood!
Instinctively looking down, Jason realised that the Cyclops had chopped off his leg using a vast amount of energy to sever through the tidal waves of energy Jason suddenly released.
Realising this, Jason roared out, as his eyes and Celestia aura turned bloody while his mind went blank.

chapters.title: Chapter 730 - Fight Of Instincts
chapters.content:
His brain abandoned all of the rational thoughts, as he was consumed with nothing but the thought of killing the peasant that had dared to cut off his leg.
Jason had yet to truly realise what had happened, but his mind had shut off before the pain could course through his entire body.
That was why he had suddenly entered a state that was solely operated by his primal instincts, and nothing else.
Crimson red eyes and a bloody red aura that held faint strands of a golden-silverish color replaced his earlier calm personality. Jason's entire demeanor and appearance had radically transformed within the blink of an eye.
The transformation was still underway as Petri's fusion, which Jason had activated since the beginning of the battle, began to intensify.
Amplified by Petri's ferocious nature, and the fact that the basilisk was the king of serpents, who couldn't stomach accepting defeat by any being, let alone the Cyclops in front of them, their rages fueled each other.
Through this, their connection intensified, and the armor of scales was growing thicker and bigger.
At the same time, Jason's reptilian eyes were piercing through the Cyclops whose face was also splattered with Jason's blood.
Seeing his own blood, Jason, who was already filled with wrath, couldn't help but switch off the logical part of his brain as the tremendous tidal waves of energy swept through his body.
After releasing one of the major seals, which the Chaos Emperor had laid on his Celestia bloodline, Jason's human blood was slowly being overpowered by the Celestia bloodline.
Yet, owing to his rage and wrath, his human half was feeling murderously angry and it only intensified further to see that the Cyclops was still alive and breathing. Wanting to end its life as soon as possible his aura flared up, sweeping through his body before being released, followed up by the activated stigma which forced the released energy to be overwhelmed and subdued in the blink of an eye.
Meanwhile, the released chaos energy was forcefully restricted, prevented from leaving his body, and channelised towards his eyes, where it was annexed without Jason realising.
Before Jason had hoped that the chaos energy, which he had absorbed after the short encounter with the Preactors, would be enough to defeat the Cyclops, but unfortunately, it hadn't been enough!
That was not because it had been too little, but rather because the Cyclops had been enveloped by a thin energy layer that didn't seem to belong to it, in the first place.
It prevented Jason from making use of his chaos attribute, and Emperor Eyes like usual, severely restricting his capabilities!
Nevertheless, now that the chaos energy he had was manifold higher, even the thin, protective energy layer around the cyclops crumbled in front of Jason's wrath. This combined the chaos energy with his abyssal effect, creating a much stronger force than Jason had ever released.
It used up the entire chaos energy Jason had just released, but before the Cyclops was able to make a single move, it had already entered the depths of the endless void of darkness.
In the end, the abyssal effect only worked for a very short moment, but that was because the Cyclops' Spiral cultivation was also at the Peak of the first threshold of the Prismar stage.
At the same time, the thin energy layer had been stronger than Jason estimated before his mind had gone blank.
Nevertheless, the short moment had been more than enough for Jason, whose body was tearing apart due to the tremendous tidal waves of energy, to appear in front of the Cyclops, barely a moment later.
It was as if he had been magically teleported before he emerged in front of the seven-meter-tall opponent, only for half a meter long claws to grow out of his knuckles, with a rapid speed almost as if they had already been prepared within his forearm.
Without thinking twice, Jason allowed Petri's fangs to grow out of his knuckles.
This was painful, but so was every single movement he made under the pressure of the enormous energy he was forced to release, in order to survive.
He had already lost a leg and Jason wanted to do nothing but kill the Cyclops, filling his entire being with rage.
The thought of turning into an Infernal Celestia didn't even cross his mind, and Jason simply let go of his emotions, releasing everything at once.
This enlarged the aura he was already releasing while his stigma began to glow in an even brighter light as the energy coursing through his body was slowly forced to obey his instructions.
His body was being invigorated by the unsealed Celestia bloodline through the sheer mass of divine energy provided which was still slowly spreading through his body. It was strengthening Jason's physique, and the amount was so high and the energy so rich that the surplus was free for Jason to dispose of.
As such, he inserted every single trace of energy that had been used to maintain the major seal into Petri's fangs that had grown out of the knuckles on the back of his hands.
All of this happened while the Cyclops was still reeling from the after-effects of his abyssal effect. It had barely begun to regain its senses, only to see that Jason, or rather, the being it assumed to have been Jason, pierced both of its hands in its one and only eye.
Unable to move fast enough, the Cyclops could only release the remaining reserves of its three energies at once.
Yet, contrary to its belief that Jason was still too weak to break through its defenses, the Cyclops comprehended that Jason's attack was completely different than before but it was too late.
The energy of the Chaos emperor got intertwined with the chaos attribute, slowly weakening the Cyclops' defenses.
Piercing Petri's fangs deep into the Cyclops' eye, Jason roared out, over-exerting his aura that had turned completely crimson in color while his eyes were slowly starting to glow in a blood-red hue.
Meanwhile, his entire wrath was channelized in his attack, through which it became stronger and stronger, only for Jason's body to become weaker by the second.
The blood loss he suffered was tremendous, yet, Jason didn't even realise anything because the adrenaline that spread through his body was numbing everything else.
Only when Petri's claws pierced through the Cyclops' eye did he slowly realise that something was off because his body was faltering all of a sudden.
Looking down, he immediately realised what was going on, which made him force the calmed down energy that coursed through his body, to seal off the bleeding from his leg, without a second of hesitation.
Somehow, Jason should have been devastated right now, but after the initial rage, he had become eerily calm as if he knew something others were oblivious to.
His entire body ached due to the tidal waves of energy that had almost torn him apart before, yet he had no time to think about the pain as he had to take care of his opponent.
With his hands deep inside the head of the Cyclops, Jason didn't even have to think about what he was going to do next.
A searing hot flame emerged around his arms and Petri's claws, rapidly spreading through the Cyclops' head.
Yet, instead of waiting for everything to end naturally, Jason released a tremendous amount of mana, to flare up Solaris' flame.
This caused the Cyclops to succumb to its inevitable fate as its head exploded, brain matter splattering through the surroundings.
With the death of the Cyclops the fight was over, and only a moment after, Jason fell to the ground, where he collapsed, deprived of the energy to continue fighting as his wrath was used up completely.
His aura and everything that had forcefully changed retracted, while the deep cut on leg continued bleeding.
Jason could only see how the part of his body that had been cut off disintegrated into countless particles before he fainted, falling right into the portal that was next to them, only to hear the artificial intelligence's voice faintly.
[10th floor successfully passed. 3 Merit points (100% speed bonus!)]
[Healing process has been initiated, Unscathed bonus deducted.]

chapters.title: Chapter 731 - Unique Regulation
chapters.content:
Upon waking up, the first thing Jason noticed was that he was still able to feel both of his legs.
This shocked him because he could swear that the last thing he fully recalled was his leg being cut off.
Recalling the memories of the fight, he began to understand what was going on.
"That's what the dungeon sees as an injury?! A leg or rather a body part being cut off???"
The pain he had felt was still imprinted deep in his mind, but that didn't prevent him from being able to think rationally.
His uncontrollable wrath about the loss of his leg had vanished, and he began to understand what was going on.
'I was clearly being overwhelmed, which forced me to unseal one of the major seals the Chaos Emperor had put on me...SO...afterward, the abyssal effect seemed to work, and now I'm...stronger, but on the verge of breaking apart because the Celestia bloodline is too potent?!'
Jason comprehended that the 'Unscathed' bonus was, in fact, the bonus he received by not losing any body part before entering the portal that led him towards the next floor.
Somehow, this was ridiculous, but Jason would be the last to complain about being able to retain his limbs.
He was glad that he wasn't a cripple anymore.
It felt as if it had never been cut off, and it was because of this that he was quite happy and relieved about what happened.
The memory was gruesome but he had learned a valuable lesson.
'Even if my body is not on the verge of breaking apart...I should really spend a few months cultivating!! The dungeon is...so much more dangerous than I expected!'
Earlier, he had been overconfident and complained that the dungeon was not representing the difficulty he had been given.
However, this idiotic thought had now disappeared, vanished into thin air, and Jason couldn't help but feel that he would be happy to have it easy in his advancement through the dungeon!
Unfortunately, that was evidently not feasible anymore.
As such, he had to find other ways to figure out a solution to his advancement through the dungeon, without being forced to loosen seals on his bloodline, let alone lose a limb.
His opinion about the dungeon was slowly changing, and Jason began to take it more seriously than before.
It was not that he was taking the dungeon lightly earlier, but he had found it to be nothing special either.
Shaking his head, when getting up from the ground, Jason felt his entire body break apart.
Clenching his fist he tried to steady himself while his skin immediately burst open, which was a bad sign.
Nevertheless, Jason was glad that his mana veins and mana core seemed to be fine. What was even better was that they had been reinforced, while the same applied to his soul world that seemed to have enlarged too!
The divine energy that had been released from the portion of his unsealed bloodline had caused this change, and Jason began to slowly understand the meaning of the minor and major seals which the Chaos Emperor had put on his bloodline.
'The minor seals restrict the Celestia race's pure energy to sweep through my body, while the major seals restrict racial traits, divine energy, and similar things from overwhelming my human bloodline…'
With the first major seal, everything seemed to have gone well, which was probably owing to his enraged human bloodline that had been caused by the emotional chaos of the loss of his leg.
Yet, at the same time, Petri's emotions had affected him the most, causing him to feel as if nobody was allowed to even touch him, let alone hurt him, creating an even more powerful impact on his emotions the moment he lost his leg.
In the end, he only won because of the major seal he released, and the aftermath was something he had to accept.
He was still alive and that was everything that mattered!
Obviously he was not well because the energy that had surged through his body had exceeded his body's limits, trying to break it apart into two, but Jason was confident that he could solve this issue now that the amount of energy within his body had been released to a certain extent.
Unfortunately, he had entered the 11th floor, which meant that he should be prepared to be attacked by other beast groups.
That had not happened when he was unconscious, or he would be dead by now, but through the Emperor Eyes, Jason could clearly see the numerous beasts around him.
Right now, he was on top of a mountain, and the temperature was well below zero degrees celsius.
Only with Solaris' help was Jason able to prevent freezing himself to death, while other beasts didn't seem to be able to reach him.
There was no flying beast, he had spotted until now.
Because of that, Jason felt reassured that it was feasible to start cultivating.
At least to the extent at which he would be able to move and fight freely without thinking that his body would tear apart at any moment.
With that in mind, Jason cultivated for an entire month to strengthen his vessel, and physique, while Petri, Spyro, and Solaris didn't stop cultivating on their own, either.
Despite cultivating relentlessly for a month straight, Jason's vessel had yet to be able to endure the multitude of amplifications he received.
As such, he was forced to continue cultivating until he could start solidifying his third prismarine crystal.
Yet, before he would be able to finish solidifying the third prismarine crystal, Jason realised that the divine energy within his body had finally been stabilised, with a small portion of it transferred to every single cell of his body.
This allowed his body to be much lighter, and after a few tests, Jason slowly comprehended that his divine energy was passively amplifying his entire being.
Understanding this was important, but also extremely interesting to figure out more about his bloodline.
There were many things he had yet to get the hang of, and the mystery about the Celestia race, his body and everything about his family continued to plague him.
In the end, it felt as if he knew nothing about himself, which was weird, but, in fact, the case.
Time would slowly help him get the hang of everything and unravel all the mysteries around him. That, Jason was absolutely certain of.
Thus, he was able to remain calm even though the mysteries of his body were sometimes frightening.
Thinking that he would figure out everything at the right time, Jason got up from the ground, the moment he finished cultivating, only to stare straight into the eyes of a fiery red tiger that had climbed up the mountain he was standing on.
For a fraction of a second, he flinched, only to realise that there was nothing to be afraid of.
There was a blizzard on top of the mountain, but instead of being utterly dumbfounded by the sudden sight of the beast, Jason smiled before he took control over his body as he kicked out with all his strength.
Mana coursed through his body, and his entire being was amplified by the divine energy within him, only to flung the tiger away that had given its all to climb up over the course of weeks.
Looking down through the mountain, Jason noticed that there were crowds of hundreds of beasts, and all of them had between seven to nine prismarine crystals.
Yet, none of them dared to approach him during his cultivation, which was weird.
But at the same time, Jason was glad about this because he didn't have to fight while being unable to control the energy surging within his body.
This had now changed, and he was more than ready to fight the crowd of beasts.
Taking a dive from the mountain with Solaris' wings spread out, Jason couldn't help but feel glad about the regeneration function of the dungeon, only to avert his attention to the beasts right in front of him.
Staring down, he started the fight against hundreds of beasts, with his soulbonds' support, and his own devastating strength.

chapters.title: Chapter 732 - Moonlight
chapters.content:
After fighting for several hours using his entire strength, Jason was exhausted, but the crowd of beasts had been obliterated.
Lying on the ground that was void of any beast, he couldn't help but feel like he had simply imagined the entire battle.
That was fortunately not the case, and he had finally adjusted himself to the advancement of strength he underwent during the last few weeks.
Jason was still not satisfied with his strength because it was not necessarily enough to pass the next few floors according to his plan.
In the end, he thought that it was best to advance to a specific rank instead of advancing through the floors in a mad rush.
Through this, his passive mana absorption could absorb mana in the time he rushed through the floors that could be liquefied until he reached the desired floor.
Afterward, it would become much easier to solidify the liquefied mana without being forced to spend additional time liquefying and absorbing mana.
With that in mind, Jason used the next four days to clear the 11th floor of all beasts, except the Guardian that had yet to emerge.
However, before clashing with the Guardian that was likely to be slightly stronger than the Cyclops, Jason wanted to solidify his third prismarine crystal.
Furthermore, he was waiting for something else to happen, thus he would rather spend his time on different things than fighting with his life on the line.
Thus, two more weeks passed, and it was only then, that Jason completed solidifying his 3rd prismarine crystal, increasing his strength by leaps and bounds!
At the same time, Petri had solidified his second prismarine crystal, and even Spyro had entered the Prismar stage!
This was an exceptional speed at which they cultivated, yet, the most shocking thing that occurred the moment Jason finished the solidification of his third prismarine crystal, was completely unexpected!
Instead of being able to finish the solidification process as it normally occured without a commotion, he faced an entirely different scenario this time.
All of a sudden, the moment Jason finished the 3rd solidified prismarine crystal, everything about his surroundings seemed to change.
Yet, the oddest was that a strange type of mana began to leak from his body that he had never felt before in his entire life! This was simply weird, but he couldn't feel his body draining of any mana despite more of this unique mana leaking from his body.
Because of that, Jason began to slowly realise that it was not him that the transmuted mana was leaking from, but rather one of his soulbonds!
In fact, it was Artemis, who had just finished her evolution!
Only a paper-thin layer of the white shroud enveloped her, but that didn't hinder the uniquely transmuted mana from leaking from her body.
Through their firm soulbond connection, it was channelised to Jason, before it began leaking from his body as well.
Escaping from his body, it slowly ascended into the air, to an extremely high altitude before it suddenly halted.
Using his Emperor Eyes, Jason tried to figure out what kind of transmutation the mana underwent, but what he knew for sure was that he had never seen such a unique transmutation before.
Despite that, he could tell that it belonged to Artemis, and an added advantage was that Jason finally understood that it was an affinity his closest soulbond had to comprehend and attain.
This was perfect, but contrary to his expectations, the affinity was different from the ice and fire affinity he already had.
It was not a normal affinity, but something that had unique effects.
As such, it was a highly rare affinity that was close to extinction.
At least, Jason assumed this based on the fact that he had never seen one of such affinities.
Yet, the moment the bright afternoon sky was replaced by a large full moon that had been conjured by the leaking mana, Jason couldn't help but smile.
"Moonlight affinity...I wonder what it can do." He was extremely interested in what Artemis had comprehended during her evolution, but Jason was even happier to think that Artemis' evolution was finally over.
He wanted to meet her again because he missed the clingy owl.
At the same time, he was curious to know just how strong she had become.
Unfortunately, his earlier excitement took a hit, the moment he sensed Artemis' strength within his soul world.
'She...is still at the exact same cultivation base? It didn't change at all?'
This confused Jason because Artemis had taken several months, just to evolve.
As such, she should have become a terrifying existence.
However, before he could spend another second blindly thinking about the intel he procured, Artemis cried out within his soul world. She was eager to spread her wings after initiating the completion of her evolution so she emerged from Jason's body, ascending into the sky.
She reached the conjured moon within no time and halted right below it before letting out a loud screech while releasing both her ice and moonlight affinity at once.
Only a moment later, Shane's eyes widened in astonishment at the sight that was revealed in front of him.
The ice Artemis had released was freezing cold, freezing the surrounding the moment it made contact with the ice.
That was already astonishing enough, considering that Artemis was still at the 4th Lique stage, but that was not what shocked him!
Earlier, the ice had a sky blue color which was now almost completely silver, intertwined with the moonlight affinity Artemis had comprehended.
This changed everything about the ice affinity's properties, enhancing it tremendously.
The freezing property became several times stronger, and so was the ice's resistance, and other characteristics received an upgrade too.
Through his Emperor Eyes, Jason could quickly evaluate that Artemis' ice affinity was strengthened by around 30%, which was an extreme enhancement.
After realising this, he couldn't help but take a second look at Artemis, whose size had decreased tremendously.
She was not a gigantic owl anymore but was twice the size of an ordinary eagle.
This was less than a fifth of her previous size, and the moment she stared at him, Jason couldn't help but smile vibrantly.
Her white wings now held traces of a faint silver color, while her sky blue eyes were now even more vibrant with a light glint of moonlight that was constantly reflected within them.
Meanwhile, the pitch-black horns on her forehead were slowly turning silver.
Seeing Artemis once again made Jason extremely happy, and even if her cultivation base didn't increase in the last few months, her strength more than made up for it.
Through the moonlight affinity, many opportunities had been unveiled, but that was not everything.
With the extremely firm connection of their soul, Jason was able to clearly sense that the majority of changes Artemis had undergone were on the inside.
Her appearance had changed quite a bit, but the time in which she had completed her evolution was more than enough for Jason to understand that her cultivation speed had increased by more than ten times.
At least, that was if the tremendous amount of mana Artemis pulled towards her, was the highest she could absorb at a time!
In the end, Jason couldn't help but think that Artemis' cultivation speed had even crossed Petri and Spyro's current speed, after the huge acceleration the cricula Minatra flowers brought forth.
Sensing this, Jason knew that Artemis would soon become his strongest soulbond once again, overshadowing the others, if they wouldn't be able to keep up with her!

chapters.title: Chapter 733 - Quarrel
chapters.content:
After Artemis evolved, Jason got a clear picture of her capabilities.
As he was thinking about her abilities, she dove towards him, clinging to Jason, as if she hadn't met him for centuries. She wrapped her wings around him, not letting him even move for a single moment.
Thus, he had to wait for quite some time before he was free again.
However, she didn't leave his side. Instead, Artemis took her usual spot on his shoulder and began using her newly attained affinity in all kinds of ways.
Testing the moonlight affinity, and what exactly it was capable of, Jason learned many new things, including that the moonlight affinity had properties related to healing, as well as enhancement of the body and affinities, which Jason had already felt before.
Through the test results, Jason got to know a lot, and he was eager to use the moonlight affinity for himself.
Unfortunately, this would take some time because the affinity seed had yet to be fully constructed in Jason's mana core.
Because of that, he had to think of a different way to approach the situation, and came up with a solution in no time!
"Let's test our fusion too!" Jason suggested, as he approached the gate that led towards the 12th Floor.
He knew that Artemis' strength was not extremely high yet, but with her fusion, he could test the moonlight affinity. Thus he was impatiently waiting as it was currently being transferred to Jason's mana core in order to let him use it actively.
However, without the comprehension and understanding of the moonlight affinity, he had to take Artemis' guidance in order to properly use it.
Excited about being able to use a new affinity after such a long time, he couldn't help but be restless as the gate opened itself.
Yet, before a beast emerged from it, Jason heard a complaint from one of his soulbonds who felt neglected because Jason was excited about Artemis' moonlight affinity.
It was Spyro, who Jason had never actively made use of before.
He spent considerable time with all of his soulbonds, but, in the end, he had no idea what Spyro could even do.
Earlier, even the Spiral Spirit had been oblivious to its capabilities, but it began grumbling the moment Jason's attention was fully focused on Artemis and her new affinity.
While Jason tried to calm down Spyro, Artemis decided to join the fray as she started to almost scream at Spyro, who couldn't help but feel offended the moment she appeared inside the soul world, proactively leaving the mana core to lecture it.
A fight was about to break out in his soul world, and Jason felt as if he was a grown-up trying to resolve a kid fight as he pulled Artemis back to his mana core, while reassuring Spyro that they would try to figure out its capabilities together.
Fortunately, the fight ended with his intervention, but Jason realised that the more soulbonds he had, the less he would use some of them actively.
For example, on Argos, he had mostly used Solaris in order to fight his opponents.
Meanwhile, right now, Solaris' flame was simply too weak to even cope with Jason's advancement speed that was tremendously high.
Even after enhancing the soul world to the highest possible capabilities, his soulbonds were unable to solidify four prismarine crystals in the time Jason solidified one unique prismarine crystal.
As such, Jason would always be faster and much stronger than them!
This was the biggest change Jason underwent since he could actively use his extremely high mana mastery to cultivate, with a strong cultivation technique by his side.
It was devastating for his soulbonds but Jason had no other choice but to continue cultivating with such a rapid speed because his strength was not even remotely close to what he wanted to reach in the near future.
There were too many powerhouses who were much stronger than he was, and even if his cultivation speed was terrifyingly high, he was already 20 years old!
If he were to face higher races, he wouldn't even be considered a prodigy to have 3 solidified prismarine crystals at the age of 20.
As such, he couldn't even remotely compare himself to his prodigious peers, if he were to encounter them.
At least if one would only judge someone's prowess from a cultivation base alone.
There were other things one had to pay attention to as well, such as the foundation of one's cultivation, and other traits, but Jason knew that he was not strong enough yet!
Because of that, he didn't want to slow down his cultivation speed, which made his soulbonds uncomfortable.
Every single loosened seal made Jason stronger and consequently turned them less useful to him.
And now that he had a combat prowess comparable to someone with more than 14 solidified prismarine crystals even without their enhancement, Jason was like a monstrous existence in the wild!
In the end, his soul energy was not a problem at all, and there was only one fear his soulbonds had, which Jason began to realise once again- their anxiety of becoming useless and unimportant to him.
This made him recall Scorpio, who had sacrificed himself, thinking that he was of no use to Jason, and had sacrificed his life to protect Jason, one last time.
Shaking his head, Jason realised that he had to find a way to allow his soulbonds to increase their strength even faster than their current speed.
Artemis' speed to cultivate should now be on par with his, possibly even higher, but that was exactly how it was ought to be.
He didn't care about binding hundreds of beasts to his soul. Rather he wanted every single beast to be able to reveal its highest capabilities and support him in achieving his goals.
At the same time, he wanted them to feel comfortable with each other, and not like any of them was stealing a spot in Jason's heart which made him love the others less, a thing that was never going to happen.
All of his soulbonds were important to him, and his decision to bind a new soulbond was always well thought, and accompanied by a good gut feeling!
Because of that, Jason didn't like the way both Spyro and Artemis were trying to be possessive, while Solaris and Petri were merely observing the scuffle in excitement as if it had nothing to do with them.
It was a ridiculous sight, but Jason couldn't feel like laughing, at all.
As such, he had to think of a solution to prevent such a scenario in the near future, but before that, Jason wanted to figure out the true capabilities of Artemis' evolution. With that thought in mind, he initiated the fusion with her just as the Guardian of the 11th Floor emerged from the gate.
Weirdly enough, it was another Cyclops that had the exact same cultivation base as the one he killed before.
This confused Jason, and if there hadn't been a slight alteration in the Cyclops' energy fluctuations, Jason would have believed that it was the exact same opponent.
However, only a moment later, Jason realised that the energy fluctuations were not the only thing that had changed.
Rather, it was the only thing he could directly perceive, only for Jason to feel targeted by a strong killing intent.
Afterward, the gravitational force around him increased a moment later, and it was then that his Emperor Eyes perceived the highly concealed affinity of the Cyclops.
'Gravitation!' He realised with a start, only to finalise his fusion with Artemis.
Black and silver-colored horns grew out of his forehead, the hair all over his body turned silver, and majestic wings sprouted out of his back.
At the same time, the Celestia aura turned icy cold, altered by Artemis' fusion.
A second stigma manifested upon Jason's first stigma, and his golden-silverish eyes turned sky-blue with a distinct silver glint in them.
The Cyclops noticed every single change that occurred within Jason, but ignoring all of it, the Cyclops emerged in front of Jason. It increased the gravitational force further, before slashing out without any mercy.
Yet, just at the same moment, Jason moved as tremendous surges of energy were released by him.
The entire surrounding froze in an instant and his eyes stared right into the Cyclops' soul as Jason said one simple word.
"Freeze!"

chapters.title: Chapter 734 - Advancing
chapters.content:
Even without the fusion with Artemis, Jason's strength had increased by leaps and bounds.
As such, the Cyclops was unable to endure the freezing cold that had been further enhanced by Jason's aura, the fully activated stigmas, the fusion, and the moonlight affinity.
Dying a painless death of being frozen alive within seconds, the Cyclops' gravitation affinity was terminated only a moment later, allowing Jason to cross the hurdle much more easily than before.
The increased gravitational force hadn't really bothered him, as he didn't even have to move after using the ice affinity that had been highly strengthened through the fusion, and the moonlight affinity.
In the end, the Guardian of the 11th floor had just died without giving Jason a proper fight, which was a stark difference to the Guardian on the 10th floor.
Through this, it was evident how much Jason's strength had increased in a span of a few months.
Given that Artemis and his other soulbonds would still increase their strength while Jason could advance through the following floors, he simply entered the 12th floor. Now that he added the additional support of Artemis, he wasn't too bothered about the slight increase in difficulty he would have to face.
While Artemis returned to the soul world, Jason forced her to befriend Spyro, with a warning that if she didn't listen, he wouldn't fuse with her anymore.
When Artemis heard this, she felt she was being bullied, and it was, in fact, exactly what Jason did.
Nevertheless, he couldn't be bothered because he needed his soulbonds to be on friendly terms with each other.
They didn't need to sacrifice their life for each other, but in order to co-exist until death, accepting each other was the bare minimum.
Jason wanted his soulbonds to be like a close family, but he couldn't force them to like each other.
As such, he would accept occasional scuffles to a certain extent before intervening.
Seeing them quarrel was not a problem, but the worse it got, the more issues would occur in the future.
It took Spyro and Artemis a while to calm down, but after the initial reason for their dislike of each other was taken away, they accepted each other and even became friendlier.
Meanwhile, Jason had already emerged on the 12th Floor and began hunting all kinds of beasts.
Until the entire floor was cleared another 10 days passed, and Jason felt like clearing the floors of all beasts took the longest.
Yet, it also gave him the time to passively cultivate and comprehend the moonlight affinity, as well as the time to adjust to his constant increase in strength, while his soulbonds could focus on cultivating.
Even if it was not necessary right now, he would require their strength latest by the 20th Floor, and considering all of their advancement, Jason was sure that the period he spent in the previous floors would be put to good use.
Improving his combat prowess while advancing his strength was the best he could do, after all!
Using all kinds of tactics to pressurise himself, Jason advanced through the 12th Floor and found it to be much easier than the 11th.
However, this was only the case because Artemis' cultivation speed exceeded Jason's expectations.
He was not sure what exactly her evolution had caused because Artemis was essentially the same, but her cultivation speed caused even Jason to feel that his advancement was slow in comparison!
In fact, Artemis could absorb and liquefy between 500-1000 drops of mana every single day!
Thus, she was able to liquefy enough mana to reach the peak of the Lique stage in a week before she would start solidifying her first prismarine crystal!
This process would take her just a week, and Jason couldn't help but feel flabbergasted because it felt like Artemis was still adjusting herself to the evolution process.
As such, she had yet to understand her capabilities to the fullest and make use of them, causing her to have a lower mana absorption rate than her limit.
After defeating the 12th Guardian by fusing with Petri, Jason had no problems in advancing further.
His earlier worry about the Guardians' strength vanished and Jason became more concerned about the fact that his vessel might be unable to cope with Artemis' advancement if she would overtake him!
The Celestia bloodline was already bothering Jason, but now Artemis' speed forced Jason to adjust his approach towards passive cultivation.
'I should start actively cultivating while running through the floors, and I can clear the beasts off the floor in between…'
Scratching the back of his head, Jason advanced to the 13th floor, followed by the 14th, 15th, all the way to the 19th floor.
Almost three and a half months had passed since Artemis evolved, and everyone was improving at a rapid pace.
Jason had solidified the fourth prismarine crystal despite being occupied with clearing the floors of all beasts while continuing to receive the speed and unscathed bonus for advancing the floors.
The Guardians from the 15th floor up had yet to reach the 2nd threshold of the Prismar stage, but their progression rate of solidifying the large rotating crystal increased exponentially with each floor.
As such, Jason knew that the Guardian of the 20th Floor was a being at the 2nd threshold.
Before, this would be something to be afraid of, but that was not the case anymore!
Artemis' tremendous cultivation speed shocked the other soulbonds, because she had not only advanced to the Prsima stage during the last 100 days but, in fact, she had been able to solidify a total of three prismarine crystals!
Jason was not sure where her sudden increment in potential came from, but the Frozen Lunarium she had devoured couldn't have been the sole reason.
In the end, he wondered if she had just compressed her body without any alteration in her potential, squeezing out every little bit, which decreased her form, but that didn't sound reasonable.
At least, Jason couldn't imagine her doing it.
However, other than that, he had no idea how evolution could make Artemis so strong.
She was a Mana eater according to the Dungeon of the Primordial Descendant, but how that trait influenced her evolution was something Jason didn't know.
Yet, rather than seeing her advancement as a disadvantage, he realised that it was obviously something good. Not only did Jason receive a tremendous increase in his strength owing to the 40% amplification of his soul world, but his other soulbonds were determined to not lose out to her!
Artemis inspired Jason to focus even more on cultivation, which was the reason he decided to alter his first sub-area!
Spyro's amplification enhanced Jason's brain functions by a large margin.
Thus, he began to modify his first sub area that was constantly absorbing mana.
This took a while and hindered him from cultivating actively with the Mythic essence technique version that allowed him to move around.
However, the results were extremely shocking because Jason was able to generate a miniature version of the Mythic essence cultivation technique within his sub-area.
As such, even without actively cultivating, his cultivation would slowly improve, and liquefied mana drops were constantly created.
To put it simply, this was extravagant, but at the same time, it was what he required to cope with Artemis' speed because she could cultivate continuously inside the soul world after he had customised it.
This hadn't been possible before her evolution, but now, after evolving, everything has changed!
As such, with a combined combat prowess that was comparable to owing more than 16 solidified prismarine crystals, without considering additional factors like the possible fusion with his soulbonds, his Emperor Eyes, and so on, Jason was finally ready to face the Guardian of the 20th Floor!

chapters.title: Chapter 735 - Duration
chapters.content:
When Jason emerged on the 20th floor, he felt a little bit weird.
The beasts' strength was much higher than that of the beast only one floor before, but even then he had no problem defeating them.
Instead, it was rather easy for him, and the amount of strength he had to use was low in comparison to before, which caused him to feel a little bit dumbfounded.
'I thought the cultivation base would increase drastically every 10th floor...did I expect too much, or did I increase my strength to a very high degree?'
The latter was not possible because one could never be too strong.
Furthermore, Jason had yet to reach the 2nd threshold of the Prismar stage. Each of his characteristics might be exceeding the 1st threshold of the Prismar stage, but, in the end, he had only solidified four prismarine crystals so far!
However, even after defeating the ferocious beasts on the 20th floor rather easily, Jason required almost an entire month just to wipe off every single beast from the floor.
It hadn't been necessary for him to do so, but in the end, even after the entire floor was cleared of beasts, Jason had yet to find the gate that led him towards the floor's Guardian and the 21st floor.
Owing to this, he launched a few more days of a detailed search without being interrupted by any kind of beasts, in which he combed through the floor, inspecting every nook and cranny.
Fortunately, it didn't take him long and the moment Jason sighted the gate, he approached it with a rapid pace. The Guardian emerged out of the opening gate, just as he crossed the required threshold.
It was a gigantic Behemoth with a height of more than 6 meters, a length of more than 20 meters, long gleaming tusks, a bulky physique, and four sturdy legs that could crush all kinds of existences under them.
However, the appearance of beasts was not something that shocked him anymore.
Rather, Jason would immediately investigate their cultivation path, cultivation base, unique traits, and other possible enhancements that were visible to his eyes.
His Emperor Eyes were constantly improving and were in sync with his advance in the cultivation ranks.
As such, he faced no issues in quickly telling what kind of advantages most beasts had.
The only issue was the concealed amplifications that the tower seemed to provide their Guardians with.
For example, the last Cyclops he fought had an extremely strong gravitation affinity that had been further enhanced through external means, while the first Cyclops had specific means to block his chaos attribute and abyssal effect to a certain extent.
Owing to these observations, he knew that the tower, or to be precise, the entire dungeon was trying to increase the difficulty to an extreme level.
However, it was exactly this scenario that caused confusion in Jason's mind because the tower's difficulty didn't seem to have increased that much from the 19th to the 20th floor.
In comparison to the difference between the 9th and 10th floor, the difference between the latter floors was not as shocking as expected. Jason could also tell that his active cultivation and that of his soulbonds must be the reason for him to feel this.
Previously, he rushed through a few floors, but that was not the case anymore.
Rather, he had cultivated for quite some time on the 11th floor, only to cultivate consistently on the following floors.
Because of that, Jason's current strength was comparable to an existence that possessed more than 20 solidified prismarine crystals!
He had yet to come across a being at the 2nd threshold of the Prismar stage, but looking deep into the Behemoth's eyes, Jason could tell that it was not as strong as he had expected it to be.
'Maybe, one of the large rotating crystals is equal to 10 solidified prismarine crystals? That's...much higher, yet lower than expected…'
Considering that one would only break through a simple threshold in the Prismar stage, a single large rotating crystal would more than double one's entire combat strength.
That was an extremely shocking boost, but Jason already possessed a combat prowess that was more than double the strength of a normal being with nine prismarine crystals.
Thus, he couldn't help but smile dryly, looking at the Behemoth that had just entered the 2nd threshold of the Prismar stage.
'Maybe I'll be able to advance a few more floors than expected?' Jason thought as he fused with Artemis, further enhancing his mana core size, and physique.
Upon receiving an amplification of 100% from Artemis' cultivation, their fusion further enhanced their strength, giving them additional enhancement as Jason's appearance began to change.
His Celestia aura was fully released before it slowly transmuted into an ice-cold aura that froze the surroundings even without supplying a single trace of mana.
Only a moment later, the two golden stigma above Jason's right eye began to glow brightly, allowing the icy cold aura to enlarge, reaching the Behemoth that did not hesitate to attack Jason.
Feeling tremendous strength radiating from Jason the moment his aura touched it, the Behemoth knew that it would die if it wouldn't do anything right now.
Thus, it charged towards Jason, causing the ground below its feet to shake violently as Byakur manifested in Jason's hand.
Making eye contact with the Behemoth, Jason's sky blue eyes seemed to rake through the Behemoth's soul. Meanwhile, Byakur was suddenly enveloped in an icy cold flame that flared up in a pale blue color with silver strands glittering on its blade.
Through the fusion with Artemis, Jason made use of the freezing flame that was forcefully transmuted from Solaris, the black origin flame, and the moonlight ability.
There was no exact degree to which the moonlight ability could enhance specific properties, but the more mana Jason inserted into it, the stronger it would become.
This was extremely beneficial, but also drained a lot of mana.
As such, Jason mostly used the moonlight ability's basic configurations because every single unique affinity, ability, and trait of his required tremendous amounts of mana.
Even after possessing four times more mana than anyone else at his cultivation base, Jason felt that he was always short of mana.
With an infinite supply of it, beasts like the Behemoth wouldn't even be able to come close to him, but unfortunately, this was not the case.
Because of that, Jason had to use Byakur to counterattack the Behemoth, whose head was lowered in an attempt to pierce its large tusks through Jason's abdomen.
Byakur had enlarged to the size of a ten-meter-long blade, and Jason didn't hesitate for a second as he thrust it at the Behemoth.
The flames followed every single movement of Byakur and the moment it collided with the Behemoth's tusks, Jason noticed that there was something he had missed out on.
"Byakur has become too weak…"
Hearing and seeing cracks sweeping over Byakur like multiple cobwebs, Jason couldn't help but sigh deeply.
He had wanted to use Byakur for a little bit longer, but that didn't seem to be possible anymore.
With that in mind, Jason realised that he would have to forge a new weapon, which was quite disappointing.
Yet, just at that moment, Byakur vibrated in reluctance as it sensed Jason's thoughts through their soul connection.
It began to glow lightly, and the cracks were forcefully halted from spreading further as if Byakur wanted to demonstrate that nothing was wrong.
Seeing this, Jason couldn't help but feel a little bit odd.
However, instead of retracting Byakur into the soul world, he exerted the Floating Sky movement technique before flapping his wings as he disappeared from his previous spot.
A moment later he emerged right below the Behemoth's head to release a tremendous amount of mana before slashing at the Guardian's head, severing it.

chapters.title: Chapter 736 - Byakur’s Value
chapters.content:
After the Guardian of the 20th Floor was defeated, Jason noticed that there was still some time before the speed bonus would run out.
At the same time, Byakur was reluctant to enter the soul world, fearing that Jason would never use it again and simply dump him inside if it were to disappear.
This caused Jason to smile dryly, wondering to what extent his soul imprint had allowed Byakur to obtain sentience.
It was an interesting sight, and Jason also realised that he couldn't simply abandon Byakur.
That wouldn't be right, even less because Byakur was a craftwork of his late master, Shane.
Furthermore, he didn't think that he could easily repeat forging a soul weapon without having refined materials for the process.
Right now, he would only be able to forge some strong weapon, but they wouldn't give him the same feeling of being an extension of his arm, let alone the same runes.
His knowledge of the three basic occupations had increased a lot since he entered Manyr, but that didn't mean that he was knowledgeable enough to create a masterpiece.
Purifying metals was an easy task for Jason because he had his eyes, Solaris and an extremely high control of mana.
As such, his weapons would always be at the Mythical grade, but that didn't mean they were as useful as Byakur!
With that in mind, Jason knew that he had to think of a solution on how he could continue to wield Byakur, without breaking it apart.
He believed that enhancing Byakur would directly transform it into a weapon that was unbreakable.
However, an unbreakable weapon was something Jason had never encountered, let alone heard of.
There were also other things he had to consider, and in the end, it was simply too frustrating to find the perfect way to retain his dagger's strength. Byakur had to remain sharp enough to pierce through the defenses of opponents, its unique abilities had to stay more effective than that of other weapons, and much more.
Because there was more than enough time before the speed bonus would wear off, Jason began to think about what he should do.
At the same time, he was simply staring at Byakur, trying to figure out a way to restore it.
If he remembered correctly, a soul weapon could be enhanced, but in order to do that, one would have to dismantle the entire weapon, and forcefully extract the soul imprints before injecting them into a different weapon.
This would be even more difficult than forging an entirely new soul weapon, with a much higher number of materials at that!
Thus, this possibility was immediately crossed out by Jason, only to recall that there was another way.
With the use of specific items, one could enhance the entire weapon.
However, Jason was not sure what kind of items they were because nobody ever mentioned them on Argos. The fact that Manyr didn't have soul weapons made it quite difficult for him to figure out more.
Thinking about possible items that could be forged into Byakur, without the need to dismantle it, or worse damage the soul imprints or runes on it, Jason realised that the requirements narrowed down the range of available choices by a large margin.
In the end, there was only one item Jason could think of within a short period of time- the Immortal eye.
If the intel he had about the Immortal eye was true, it was a nearly indestructible item that was used for various things owing to its wide range of characteristics.
Yet, most of the uses had to do with the forging process of extremely strong weapons, armors, or items that required tremendous energy storage space to be even used.
To put it simply, it was a versatile item that every blacksmith knew and desired to forge with.
Unfortunately, Jason had never used an Immortal eye. Thus, he couldn't be sure what he had to pay attention to if he were to forge with it, let alone if it was even possible to connect it with Byakur.
Initially, he took the Immortal eye with him because he was going to hand it over to Luna, who required it for something.
However, after giving it a second thought he realised that his current situation was more important than saving something for a person he might never see again.
In the end, Jason was still in the first trial of the Dungeon of the Primordial Descendant.
Furthermore, the first trial was going to last for more than a year.
Adding the subsequent trials, Jason was sure that a few more years would pass.
It was annoying, and he couldn't help but feel a little bit frustrated because there were too many things he had planned to do, such as receiving the Mythic Essence cultivation technique from Luna, as well as training and spending time with Jennifer.
The last thought astonished Jason for a moment, only to shake his head.
'I will definitely see them again, but someone else will probably take care of the Immortal eye, right? Even if that's not the case, Byakur will break if I continue using it without any enhancements!'
Byakur was not only his soul weapon, but its entire existence had a special place in his heart because it was one of the last things that was left of his late masters.
Because of that, Jason would love to continue using it, even if it meant that he would have to break his promise with Luna.
In the end, Jason was still unsure what Luna would be doing with the Immortal eye, to begin with, because her expression while talking about it was not good.
Recalling the glint of pure wrath within the depths of her eyes, Jason made up his mind, telling himself that it was more important to ensure his survival, and Byakur was the best means to allow him to execute the strongest possible combat prowess.
He could change its length as per his wish and it had all kinds of useful abilities.
Additionally, his soulbonds could easily access Byakur too because everything was connected to his soul.
Thus, amplifying Byakur with their affinities was extremely easy.
The more Jason thought about Byakur's value, the less was his desire to simply replace it with another, possibly stronger weapon.
After coming to a conclusion, Jason decided to break his promise to Luna.
If possible, he would simply take another Immortal eye as his reward once the dungeon trials were over.
This made him feel less guilty, and he thus accessed his spatial ring before taking out the Immortal eye.
Before, he hadn't even given it a second glance because the Immortal eye had been useless to him.
However, now the situation had changed drastically.
Inserting a large amount of mana in his Emperor eyes, he looked at the Immortal eye closely, holding it straight in front of his eye.
This allowed him to see inside the Immortal eye's in an extremely detailed manner.
What he saw astonished him greatly because the overly compressed things he could see inside the Immortal eye were on a completely different level than materials at the Prismar, or even Ascendion stage.
Yet, instead of feeling that this was great, Jason couldn't help but feel a little bit concerned.
'Will I even be able to reach a high enough temperature to melt the Immortal eye?!'
However, fortunately, this thought was proven to be groundless the moment he took out the portable smithy, in addition to every single tool he required to hopefully improve Byakur's strength!
